And in it: "naqa durur," that is, abundant in milk. And in it: "al-nathur," that is, abundant in offspring.
2. . His statement "nor the restrainers (al-waza'a)": plural of "wazi'," the one who holds back from harm, and the one who steps ahead of the line and sets it right by moving forward and back. Stated in al-Sihah. (Ayn)
1. (1) . قوله لم يحل منه بكثير طائل» في الصحاح: قولهم «لم يحل منه بطائل» أى: لم يستفد منه كبير فائدة وفيه: اللقح- بالكسر-: الإبل بأعيانها، الواحدة: لقوح، وهي الحلوب، مثل: فلوص وقلاص: واللقحة: اللقوح، والجمع لقح مثل قربة قرب، وفيه: ناقة درور، أى: كثيرة اللبن. وفيه: النثور، أى: كثيرة الولد.
2. . قوله «ولا الوزعة» جمع وازع، وهو الذي يكف عن الضرر، والذي يتقدم الصف فيصلحه بالتقديم والتأخير. أفاده الصحاح. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 91
1. (1) . His statement "and it has been read 'ni'ma al-'abd' on the original form": perhaps with fatha on the nun and kasra on the 'ayn, as al-Sihah indicates. (Ayn)
2. . By Imru' al-Qays. It is also said: by al-'Ajjaj, describing a horse. "Al-sufun" — with the undotted letter — is standing on the tip of the hoof of a fore or hind leg. "Al-sunbuk" is the tip of the horse's hoof. "Al-sufun" — with the dotted letter — is bringing the forelegs together in standing. "Mimma yaqumu" is the predicate of "kana," that is: he loved the standing, as if he were of the kind that stands on three legs. Or as if he were created from standing on three, as man was created from haste, being broken in the fourth leg, or breaking it, that is, its second; so "ma" is relative or infinitive. And "kasiran" is a circumstantial clause, and the sentence is the predicate of "yazalu"; and this is what the opinion of Ibn al-Hajib settled on in the Amali after a long discussion. Had you made "ma" infinitive and "kasiran" the predicate of "ka'anna," its right would be the nominative; and had you made it the predicate of "yazalu," as Ibn Hisham preferred, the meaning would be: "so he does not cease broken, as if he were of those who stand on three," as has passed. It is also possible that the meaning is: "so he does not cease broken from his standing on three," and "ka'anna" is parenthetical, its predicate omitted, that is, "as if he were broken"; its benefit is precaution.
3. . I did not find it in this form; in the Sunan is the hadith of Mu'awiya: "Whoever is pleased that people stand up before him." And in al-Gharib of Abu Ubayd, from the hadith of al-Bara' ؓ: "When we prayed with the Messenger of God ﷺ and he raised his head, we stood with him in rows."
4. . His statement "after he had prayed the first prayer on his throne": the wording of al-Nasafi: "he prayed the noon prayer." (Ayn)
1. (1) . قوله «وقرئ نعم العبد على الأصل» لعله بفتح النون وكسر العين، كما يفيده الصحاح. (ع)
2. . لامرئ القيس. وقيل: للعجاج يصف فرسا. والصفون- بالمهملة-: الوقوف على سنبك يد أو رجل. والسنبك: طرف حافر الفرس. والصفون- بالمعجمة-: الجمع بين اليدين في الوقوف، ومما يقوم: خبر كان، أى: أحب الصفون، كأنه من الجنس الذي يقوم على ثلاث قوائم. أو كأنه مخلوق من القيام على ثلاثة كخلق الإنسان من عجل، حال كونه مكسور القائمة الرابعة، أو كاسرها أى ثانيها، فما موصولة أو مصدرية. وكسيرا: حال، والجملة: خبر يزال، وهذا ما استقر عليه رأى ابن الحاجب في الأمالى بعد كلام طويل، ولو جعلت ما مصدرية، وكسيرا: خبر كأن، كان حقه الرفع، ولو جعلته خبر يزال كما اختاره ابن هشام، لكان المعنى: فلا يزال كسيرا، كأنه مما يقوم على الثلاث على ما مر. ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: فلا يزال كسيرا من قيامه على الثلاث، وكأنه اعتراض، وخبره محذوف، أى كأنه كسير. وفائدته الاحتراس.
3. . لم أجده هكذا وفي السنن حديث معاوية «من سره أن يتمثل الناس له قياما» وفي الغريب لأبى عبيد من حديث البراء رضى الله عنه «كنا إذا صلينا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فرفع رأسه قمنا معه صفوفا.
4. . قوله «بعد ما صلى الأولى على كرسيه» عبارة النسفي. صلى الظهر. (ع)
17
Q 38:30–33 · Vol. 4, pp. 91–93

Verses 30 to 33

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And We gave to David Solomon. An excellent servant! Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning back [to God] (30) [Mention] when there were displayed before him in the afternoon the poised, swift steeds (31) And he said, "Indeed, I gave preference to the love of good things over the remembrance of my Lord until [the sun] disappeared into the curtain [of darkness] (32) Return them to me," and he began passing [his hand] over [their] legs and necks (33)
وَوَهَبْنا لِداوُدَ سُلَيْمانَ نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ (30) إِذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِالْعَشِيِّ الصَّافِناتُ الْجِيادُ (31) فَقالَ إِنِّي أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّي حَتَّى تَوارَتْ بِالْحِجابِ (32) رُدُّوها عَلَيَّ فَطَفِقَ مَسْحاً بِالسُّوقِ وَالْأَعْناقِ (33)
Vol. 4, p. 91
It has been read "ni'ma al-'abd" on the original form «1», and the one specified for praise is omitted. And He gave as the reason for his being praised that he was "awwab," one who often returns to Him with repentance; or one who glorifies, who echoes the glorification, because every "mu'awwib" is "awwab." "Al-safin" is the one in the saying: "He grew used to standing, so he does not cease, as if from standing on three he were broken." «2» It is also said: the one who stands on the tip of the hoof of a fore or hind leg is the "mutakhayyim"; as for the "safin," it is the one who brings his forelegs together. From the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever is pleased that people stand in rows (sufunan) for him, let him take his seat in the Fire" «3», that is: standing, as they serve tyrants.
وقرئ: نعم العبد، على الأصل، «1» والمخصوص بالمدح محذوف. وعلل كونه ممدوحا بكونه أوّابا رجاعا إليه بالتوبة. أو مسبحا مؤوّبا للتسبيح مرجعا له، لأن كل مؤوّب أوّاب. والصافن: الذي في قوله: ألف الصّفون فما يزال كأنّه … ممّا يقوم على الثّلاث كسيرا «2» وقيل: الذي يقوم على طرف سنبك يد أو رجل: هو المتخيم. وأما الصافن: فالذي يجمع بين يديه. وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «من سره أن يقوم الناس له صفونا فليتبوّأ مقعده من النار» «3» أى: واقفين كما خدم الجبابرة.
Question
If you say: What is the meaning of describing them with standing (sufun)?
فإن قلت: ما معنى وصفها بالصفون؟
Answer
I say: sufun is hardly found in cross-breeds; it is only in the pure Arabians. It is also said: He described them with standing and excellence, to combine for them the two praiseworthy descriptions, standing and running, meaning: when they stand, they are calm and settled in their standing places, and when they run, they are swift and light in their running. It is reported that Solomon ﷺ raided the people of Damascus and Nisibis and took a thousand horses. It is also said: he inherited them from his father, who had obtained them from the Amalekites. It is also said: they came out of the sea, having wings; and one day, after he had prayed the first prayer, he sat on his throne «4» and reviewed them, and did not
قلت: الصفون لا يكاد يكون في الهجن، وإنما هو في العراب الخلص. وقيل: وصفها بالصفون والجودة، ليجمع لها بين الوصفين المحمودين: واقفة وجارية، يعنى: إذا وقفت كانت ساكنة مطمئنة في مواقفها، وإذا جرت كانت سراعا خفافا في جريها. وروى أن سليمان عليه السلام غزا أهل دمشق ونصيبين، فأصاب ألف فرس. وقيل: ورثها من أبيه وأصابها أبوه من العمالقة. وقيل: خرجت من البحر لها أجنحة، فقعد يوما بعد ما صلى الأولى على كرسيه «4» واستعرضها، فلم
Vol. 4, p. 92
cease being displayed to him until the sun set, and he was heedless of the afternoon prayer, or of a recital of remembrance he had at evening time, and they were in awe of him and did not inform him; so he was distressed at what he had missed, and had them brought back and hamstrung them, drawing near «1» to God, and a hundred remained, so whatever fine horses remain in people's hands are from their offspring. It is also said: when he hamstrung them, God replaced them with something better, which is the wind running at his command.
تزل تعرض عليه حتى غربت الشمس وغفل عن العصر أو عن ورد من الذكر كان له وقت العشى، وتهيبوه فلم يعلموه، فاغتم لما فاته، فاستردها وعقرها مقربا «1» لله، وبقي مائة، فما بقي في أيدى الناس من الجياد فمن نسلها، وقيل: لما عقرها أبدله الله خيرا منها، وهي الريح تجرى بأمره.
Question
If you say: What is the meaning of "I gave preference to the love of good things over the remembrance of my Lord"?
فإن قلت: ما معنى أَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّي؟
Answer
I say: "ahbabtu" is imbued with the meaning of a verb that is transitive with "'an," as if it were said: "I made the love of good stand in place of the remembrance of my Lord"; or: "I made the love of good suffice or dispense with the remembrance of my Lord." And Abu al-Fath al-Hamadani mentioned in the book al-Tibyan that "ahbabtu" means "I clung to," as in: "like the bad camel when it knelt (ahabba)" «2», but it is not so. And "al-khayr" is wealth, as in His saying "if he leaves behind good (khayr)" and His saying "and indeed he is, in love of good, intense"; and the wealth is the horses that occupied him. Or he called the horses "khayr" as though they were the very self of good, because good is attached to them. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Good is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection" «3», and he said of Zayd al-Khayl when he came to him as a delegate and became Muslim: "No man was described to me and then I saw him but that he was less than what had reached me, except Zayd al-Khayl" «4», and he named him Zayd al-Khayr. A man asked Bilal ؓ about people who were racing: "Who was first?" He said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ." The man said to him: "I meant the horses." He said: "And I meant the good (khayr)." «5»
قلت: أحببت: مضمن معنى فعل يتعدى بعن، كأنه قيل: أنبت حب الخير عن ذكر ربى. أو جعلت حب الخير مجزيا أو مغنيا عن ذكر ربى. وذكر أبو الفتح الهمداني في كتاب التبيان: أن «أحببت» بمعنى: لزمت، من قوله: مثل بعير السوء إذ أحبّا «2» وليس بذاك. والخير: المال، كقوله إِنْ تَرَكَ خَيْراً وقوله وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ والمال: الخيل التي شغلته. أو سمى الخيل خيرا كأنها نفس الخير لتعلق الخير بها. قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «الخيل معقود بنواصيها الخير إلى يوم القيامة «3» » وقال في زيد الخيل حين وفد عليه وأسلم: «ما وصف لي رجل فرأيته إلا كان دون ما بلغني إلا زيد الخيل» «4» وسماه زيد الخير. وسأل رجل بلالا رضى الله عنه عن قوم يستبقون: من السابق؟ فقال: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم. فقال له الرجل: أردت الخيل. فقال: وأنا أردت الخير «5» .
Vol. 4, p. 93
"Disappearing behind the curtain" is a figure of speech for the setting of the sun, [taken] from the disappearance of the king. Or [the meaning is] the one hidden by their curtain. What indicates that the pronoun refers to the sun is that the mention of the evening has passed, and a pronoun must have a preceding mention or an indication of mention. It is also said: the pronoun refers to the steeds, that is: until they disappeared behind the curtain of night, meaning darkness. Among the innovations of the interpretations: that the "curtain" is a mountain beyond Qaf, a year's journey away, behind which the sun sets. "So he began passing [his hand] (masḥan)": he proceeded to wipe, that is, to wipe with the sword over their legs and necks, meaning to cut them. One says: "masaha 'ilawatahu" when he struck his neck, and "masaha al-musfir al-kitab" «1» when he cut off its edges with his sword. From al-Hasan: he cut their hamstrings and struck their necks; he meant by "kasf" cutting, from which comes "al-kasf" among the epithets of the metrical alterations in prosody. Whoever says it with the dotted shin is mistaken. It is also said: he wiped them with his hand in admiration and being impressed with them.
والتواري بالحجاب: مجاز في غروب الشمس عن توارى الملك. أو المخبأة بحجابهما. والذي دل على أن الضمير للشمس مرور ذكر العشى، ولا بد للمضمر من جرى ذكر أو دليل ذكر. وقيل: الضمير للصافنات، أى: حتى توارت بحجاب الليل يعنى الظلام. ومن بدع التفاسير: أن الحجاب جبل دون قاف بمسيرة سنة تغرب الشمس من ورائه فَطَفِقَ مَسْحاً فجعل يمسح مسحا، أى يمسح بالسيف بسوقها وأعناقها، يعنى: يقطعها. يقال: مسح علاوته، إذا ضرب عنقه، ومسح المسفر الكتاب «1» إذا قطع أطرافه بسيفه. وعن الحسن: كسف عراقيبها وضرب أعناقها، أراد بالكسف: القطع، ومنه: الكسف في ألقاب الزحاف في العروض. ومن قاله بالشين المعجمة فمصحف. وقيل: مسحها بيده استحسانا لها وإعجابا بها.
Question
If you say: To what is "Return them to me" connected?
فإن قلت: بم اتصل قوله رُدُّوها عَلَيَّ؟
Answer
I say: to an omitted [verb] whose estimation is: "he said: return them to me," so he omitted it and omitted what is the answer to it, as if a questioner said: "And what did Solomon say?" because it is a place that plainly calls for the question, namely the occupation of one of God's prophets with a worldly matter until the prayer escapes him past its time. It has been read "bil-su'q" with hamza on the waw because of its damma, as in "adur"; its like is "al-ghu'ur" as the verbal noun of "gharat al-shams." As for whoever read "bil-suq," he made the damma in the sin as though it were on the waw, for adjacency, as one says "mu'sa"; and the like of "saq" and "suq" is "asad" and "usd." And it has been read "bil-saq," content with the singular in place of the plural, for safety from confusion.
قلت: بمحذوف تقديره: قال ردّوها علىّ، فأضمر وأضمر ما هو جواب له، كأن قائلا قال: فماذا قال سليمان؟ لأنه موضع مقتض للسؤال اقتضاء ظاهرا، وهو اشتغال نبىّ من أنبياء الله بأمر الدنيا، حتى تفوته الصلاة عن وقتها. وقرئ: بالسؤق، بهمز الواو لضمتها، كما في أدؤر. ونظيره: الغئور، في مصدر غارت الشمس. وأما من قرأ بالسؤق فقد جعل الضمة في السين كأنها في الواو للتلاصق، كما قيل: مؤسى: ونظير ساق وسوق: أسد وأسد. وقرئ: بالساق، اكتفاء بالواحد عن الجمع، لأمن الإلباس.

Vol. 4, p. 92
1. (1) . His statement "and he hamstrung them, drawing near (muqarraban) to God": the wording of al-Nasafi: "taqarruban." (Ayn)
2. . "Kayfa qarrabta 'amma-ka al-qarshaba / hina ataka laghiban mukhibban / hultu 'alayhi bil-qafili darban / tabban liman bil-hawni qad alabba / mithla ba'iri al-su'i idh ahabba" by Abu Muhammad al-Fa'qasi. "Al-qarshab" — with kasra on the first and fatha on the third — is the aged; "al-laghib" is from "lughub," which is fatigue; "al-mukhibb" is from "akhabbahu" when he made him go at the "khabab," a kind of walking; or from "akhabba" when he stuck to the place, as has been said. "Hultu," that is, I stood and sprang upon him. "Al-qafil" is the whip. "Darban" is in the sense of "darib(an)," or "you strike him a striking." "Al-tabb" is perdition, and it is a supplication against him, whose verb is omitted obligatorily. "Al-hawn" — with damma — is humiliation. "Alabba bil-makan": he stayed in it. Al-Asma'i narrated it thus: "Kayfa qarrabta shaykhaka al-adhaba / lamma ataka yabisan qarshaban / qumta 'alayhi bil-qafili darban / mithla ba'iri al-su'i idh ahabba." And "al-dhayb" is abundance and length of hair; and "al-adhab" is the camel on whose brows hairs have grown, so that when the wind strikes it, it bolts and surges. Al-Jawhari said: "al-ikhbab" is kneeling; and in camels it is like balking in horses.
3. . Agreed upon, from the hadith of Ibn Umar ؓ both.
4. . Mentioned by Ibn Ishaq in the Maghazi without a chain, and by al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il from his route. And Ibn Sa'd mentioned it from al-Waqidi with severed chains of his.
5. . Narrated by Ibrahim al-Harbi from the narration of Mughira from al-Sha'bi, who said: "There was a race. A man said to Bilal: Who was first? He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ. He said: Then who came second? He said: Abu Bakr. He said: I only meant among the horses. He said: And I meant among the good."
1. (1) . قوله «وعقر ما مقربا لله» عبارة النسفي: تقربا. (ع)
2. . كيف قربت عمك القرشبا
…. حين أتاك لاغبا مخبا حلت عليه بالقفيل ضربا
…. تبا لمن بالهون قد ألبا مثل بعير السوء إذ أحبا لأبى محمد الفقعسي. والقرشب- بكسر أوله وفتح ثالثه-: المسن، واللاغب، من اللغوب: وهو التعب. والمخب من أخبه: إذا حمله على الخبب، وهو نوع من السير. أو من أخب: إذا لزم المكان كما قيل. وحلت: أى قمت ووثبت عليه. والقفيل: السوط. وضربا: بمعنى ضاربا. أو تضربه ضربا. والتب: الهلاك، وهو دعاء عليه، وفعله محذوف وجوبا. والهون- بالضم-: الهوان. وألب بالمكان: أقام به، ورواه الأصمعى هكذا: كيف قربت شيخك الأذبا
…. لما أتاك يابسا قرشبا قمت عليه بالقفيل ضربا
…. مثل بعير السوء إذ أحبا والذيب: كثرة الشعر وطوله. والأذب: البعير الذي نبت على حاجبيه شعيرات، فإذا ضربته الريح نفر وماج. وقال الجوهري: الاخباب: البروك. وهو في الإبل كالحران في الخبل.
3. . متفق عليه من حديث ابن عمر رضى الله عنهما.
4. . ذكره ابن إسحاق في المغازي بغير سند، والبيهقي في الدلائل من طريقه. وذكره ابن سعد عن الواقدي بأسانيد له مقطوعة

Q 38:34 · Vol. 4, pp. 93–95

Verse 34

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And We certainly tried Solomon and placed on his throne a body; then he repented (34)
وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا سُلَيْمانَ وَأَلْقَيْنا عَلى كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَداً ثُمَّ أَنابَ (34)
Vol. 4, p. 93
It is said: Solomon was tried after he had reigned twenty years, and he reigned after the trial twenty years. Part of his trial was: a son was born to him, so the devils said: if he lives we shall not be freed from forced labor, so our way is to kill him or madden him; he learned of that, so he used to feed him in the clouds «2», and he was startled only to find him cast dead on his throne; so he became aware of his mistake, in that he did not rely on his Lord regarding him, so he asked forgiveness of his Lord and repented to Him. It is reported from the Prophet ﷺ: "Solomon said: Tonight I will go around to seventy women, each of whom will bring a horseman fighting in the way of God," and he did not say "if God wills"; so he went around to them and only one woman conceived, who brought forth half a man. "By Him in whose hand is my soul, had he said 'if God wills,' they would all have fought in the way of God as horsemen." «3» So that is His saying "And We certainly tried Solomon." And this and the like of it is without harm. As for what is narrated of the story of the ring, the devils, and the worship of
قيل: فتن سليمان بعد ما ملك عشرين سنة. وملك بعد الفتنة عشرين سنة. وكان من فتنته: أنه ولد له ابن، فقالت الشياطين: إن عاش لم ننفك من السخرة، فسبيلنا أن نقتله أو نخبله، فعلم ذلك، فكان يغذوه في السحابة «2» فما راعه إلا أن ألقى على كرسيه ميتا، فتنبه على خطئه في أن لم يتوكل فيه على ربه، فاستغفر ربه وتاب إليه. وروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: قال سليمان: لأطوفن الليلة على سبعين امرأة، كل واحدة تأتى بفارس يجاهد في سبيل الله، ولم يقل: إن شاء الله، فطاف عليهنّ فلم يحمل إلا امرأة واحدة جاءت بشق رجل، والذي نفسي بيده، لو قال: إن شاء الله، لجاهدوا في سبيل الله فرسانا أجمعون «3» ، فذلك قوله تعالى وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا سُلَيْمانَ. وهذا ونحوه مما لا بأس به. وأما ما يروى من حديث الخاتم والشياطين وعبادة
Vol. 4, p. 94
the idol in Solomon's house, God knows best of its soundness «1»: they related that news reached Solomon of Sidon, a city on one of the islands, and that in it was a king of great standing who could not be overcome because of his fortification by the sea; so he set out to him, the wind carrying him until he alighted there with his troops of jinn and humans, killed its king, and took a daughter of his named Jarada, among the most beautiful of people in face; so he chose her for himself, and she became Muslim and he loved her; and her tears never ceased from grief for her father; so he commanded the devils, who fashioned for her an image of her father, and she clothed it like his clothing; and she would go to it morning and evening with her maidservants, who prostrated to it as was their custom in his kingdom. Asaf informed Solomon of that, so he broke the image and punished the woman. Then he went out alone into the wilderness and ashes were spread for him, and he sat upon them, repentant to God, humbling himself. He had a concubine, mother of a child, called Amina; when he went in for purification or to be with a woman, he placed his ring with her, and his kingdom was in his ring. One day he placed it with her, and the devil of the sea came to her — he who showed Solomon the diamond when he ordered the building of the Holy House, named Sakhr — in the form of Solomon and said: "O Amina, my ring," and he put the ring on and sat on Solomon's throne; the birds, jinn and humans gathered around him, and Solomon was changed from his appearance. He came to Amina to ask for the ring, but she denied him and drove him away; so he knew that the sin had overtaken him. He used to go round the houses begging, and when he said: "I am Solomon," they showered him with dust and cursed him. Then he went to the fishermen, carrying fish for them, and they would give him two fish a day, and he stayed so for forty mornings, the number of days the idol was worshipped in his house. Asaf and the great ones of the Children of Israel disapproved of the devil's rule, and Asaf asked Solomon's wives; they said: "He does not leave any one of us in her menstrual blood, and he does not wash from sexual impurity." It is also said: rather his rule was effected in everything except them. Then the devil flew off and threw the ring into the sea, and a fish swallowed it, and the fish fell into Solomon's hand; he split open its belly and there was the ring; he put it on and fell prostrate, and his kingdom returned to him; and he hewed a rock for Sakhr «2» and put him in it, and sealed it with another, then bound them with iron and lead and cast him into the sea. It is also said: when he was tried, the ring would fall from his hand, not staying in it; so Asaf said to him: "You are tried by your sin and the ring does not stay in your hand, so repent to God Almighty." The accomplished scholars refused to accept it and said: this is from the falsehoods of the Jews; the devils cannot do the like of these deeds. And God's giving them power over His servants so that they fall into changing rulings, and over the wives of prophets so as to commit fornication with them, is repugnant. As for the making of statues, laws may differ about it. Do you not see His saying "of sanctuaries and statues"? As for prostration to the image, it is not to be thought that the Prophet of God would permit it; and if it was without his knowledge, he is not to blame. And His saying "and We placed on his throne a body" is evidently remote from conveying the meaning of the devil's being installed in his place.
الوثن في بيت سليمان، فالله أعلم بصحته «1» حكوا أن سليمان بلغه خبر صيدون وهي مدينة في بعض الجزائر، وأنّ بها ملكا عظيم الشأن لا يقوى عليه لتحصنه بالبحر، فخرج إليه تحمله الريح حتى أناخ بها بجنوده من الجن والإنس، فقتل ملكها وأصاب بنتا له اسمها جرادة من أحسن الناس وجها، فاصطفاها لنفسه وأسلمت وأحبها، وكانت لا يرقأ دمعها حزنا على أبيها، فأمر الشياطين فمثلوا لها صورة أبيها، فكستها مثل كسوته وكانت تغدو إليها وتروح مع ولائدها يسجدن له كعادتهنّ في ملكه، فأخبر آصف سليمان بذلك فكسر الصورة وعاقب المرأة، ثم خرج وحده إلى فلاة وفرش له الرماد، فجلس عليه تائبا إلى الله متضرّعا، وكانت له أمّ ولد يقال لها أمينة، إذا دخل للطهارة أو لإصابة امرأة وضع خاتمه عندها، وكان ملكه في خاتمه، فوضعه عندها يوما وأتاها الشيطان صاحب البحر- وهو الذي دلّ سليمان على الماس حين أمر ببناء بيت المقدس واسمه صخر- على صورة سليمان فقال: يا أمينة خاتمي، فتختم به وجلس على كرسي سليمان، وعكفت عليه الطير والجنّ والإنس، وغير سليمان عن هيئته فأتى أمينة لطلب الخاتم فأنكرته وطردته، فعرف أنّ الخطيئة قد أدركته، فكان يدور على البيوت يتكفف، فإذا قال: أنا سليمان حثوا عليه التراب وسبوه، ثم عمد إلى السماكين ينقل لهم السمك فيعطونه كلّ يوم سمكتين، فمكث على ذلك أربعين صباحا عدد ما عبد الوثن في بيته، فأنكر آصف وعظماء بنى إسرائيل حكم الشيطان، وسأل آصف نساء سليمان فقلنا: ما يدع امرأة منا في دمها ولا يغتسل من جنابة. وقيل: بل نفذ حكمه في كل شيء إلا فيهنّ، ثم طار الشيطان وقذف الخاتم في البحر، فابتلعته سمكة ووقعت السمكة في يد سليمان، فبقر بطنها فإذا هو بالخاتم، فتختم به ووقع ساجدا، ورجع إليه ملكه، وجاب صخرة لصخر «2» فجعله فيها، وسدّ عليه بأخرى ثم أوثقهما بالحديد والرصاص وقذفه في البحر. وقيل: لما افتتنن كان يسقط الخاتم من يده لا يتماسك فيها، فقال له آصف: إنك لمفتون بذنبك والخاتم لا يقرّ في يدك، فتب إلى الله عز وجل. ولقد أبى العلماء المتقنون قبوله وقالوا: هذا من أباطيل اليهود، والشياطين لا يتمكنون من مثل هذه الأفاعيل. وتسليط الله إياهم على عباده حتى يقعوا في تغيير الأحكام، وعلى نساء الأنبياء حتى يفجروا بهنّ: قبيح، وأما اتخاذ التماثيل فيجوز أن تختلف فيه الشرائع. ألا ترى إلى قوله مِنْ مَحارِيبَ وَتَماثِيلَ وأما السجود للصورة فلا يظن بنبىّ الله أن يأذن فيه، وإذا كان بغير علمه فلا عليه. وقوله وَأَلْقَيْنا عَلى كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَداً ناب عن إفادة معنى إنابة الشيطان منابه نبوّا ظاهرا.

Q 38:35 · Vol. 4, p. 95

Verse 35

The verse as the commentary quotes it
He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower" (35)
قالَ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَهَبْ لِي مُلْكاً لا يَنْبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِنْ بَعْدِي إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ (35)
Vol. 4, p. 95
He put seeking forgiveness before asking for the kingdom, in keeping with the custom of the prophets and the righteous in putting the matter of their religion before the matters of their worldly life. "La yanbaghi": is not easy and does not occur. And the meaning of "from after me (min ba'di)" is "other than me (duni)."
قدّم الاستغفار على استيهاب الملك جريا على عادة الأنبياء والصالحين في تقديمهم أمر دينهم على أمور دنياهم لا يَنْبَغِي لا يتسهل ولا يكون. ومعنى مِنْ بَعْدِي دوني.
Question
If you say: Does it not resemble envy and greed to monopolize a blessing, to ask God for what He does not give to others?
فإن قلت: اما يشبه الحسد والحرص على الاستبداد بالنعمة أن يستعطى الله ما لا يعطيه غيره؟
Answer
I say: Solomon ﷺ was raised in a house of kingship and prophethood and was heir to both, so he wanted to ask his Lord for a miracle, and he asked, according to his familiarity, for a kingdom exceeding other kingdoms with an extraordinary excess reaching the limit of miracle, so that it would be proof of his prophethood overpowering those he was sent to, and so that it would be a miracle breaking customs; that is the meaning of His saying "will not belong to anyone after me." It is also said: it was a great kingdom, and he feared that the like would be given to someone who would not maintain God's limits in it, as the angels said "Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we glorify You with praise and sanctify You?" It is also said: a kingdom that I will not be stripped of and in which no one other than me will take my place, as I was stripped of it once and another was set in my place. It is also possible to say: God knew in what He specified for him of that great kingdom benefits for religion, and knew that no one other than he would bear its burdens, and wisdom required his asking for it, so He commanded him to ask Him for it, and he asked for it by God's command, in the manner God knew no one could manage except him alone, without His other servants. Or he wanted to say "a great kingdom," so he said "will not belong to anyone after me," and did not intend by that except the greatness and breadth of the kingdom, as you say: "So-and-so has what no one has of virtue and wealth," while perhaps people have the like of that, but you intend to magnify what he has. From al-Hajjaj: it was said to him: "You are envious," and he said: "More envious than I is the one who said 'grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me,'" and this is of his audacity against God and his devilishness, as is related of him: "Our obedience is more obligatory than obedience to God, because He made a condition in His obedience, saying 'So fear God as much as you are able,' and left ours unrestricted, saying 'and those in authority among you.'"
قلت: كان سليمان عليه السلام ناشئا في بيت الملك والنبوّة ووارثا لهما، فأراد أن يطلب من ربه معجزة، فطلب على حسب ألفه ملكا زائدا على الممالك زيادة خارقة للعادة بالغة حد الإعجاز، ليكون ذلك دليلا على نبوّته قاهرا للمبعوث إليهم، وأن يكون معجزة حتى يخرق العادات، فذلك معنى قوله لا يَنْبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِنْ بَعْدِي وقيل: كان ملكا عظيما، فخاف أن يعطى مثله أحد فلا يحافظ على حدود الله فيه، كما قالت الملائكة أَتَجْعَلُ فِيها مَنْ يُفْسِدُ فِيها وَيَسْفِكُ الدِّماءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ وقيل: ملكا لا أسلبه ولا يقوم غيرى فيه مقامي، كما سلبته مرّة وأقيم مقامي غيرى. ويجوز أن يقال: علم الله فيما اختصه به من ذلك الملك العظيم مصالح في الدين، وعلم أنه لا يضطلع بأعبائه غيره، وأوجبت الحكمة استيهابه، فأمره أن يستوهبه إياه، فاستوهبه بأمر من الله على الصفة التي علم الله أنه لا يضبطه عليها إلا هو وحده دون سائر عباده. أو أراد أن يقول ملكا عظيما فقال لا يَنْبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِنْ بَعْدِي، ولم يقصد بذلك إلا عظم الملك وسعته، كما تقول: لفلان ما ليس لأحد من الفضل والمال، وربما كان للناس أمثال ذلك، ولكنك تريد تعظيم ما عنده. وعن الحجاج أنه قيل له: إنك حسود، فقال: أحسد منى من قال هَبْ لِي مُلْكاً لا يَنْبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِنْ بَعْدِي وهذا من جرأته على الله وشيطنته، كما حكى عنه: طاعتنا أوجب من طاعة الله، لأنه شرط في طاعته فقال فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ وأطلق طاعتنا فقال وَأُولِي الْأَمْرِ مِنْكُمْ.

Q 38:36–40 · Vol. 4, pp. 95–96

Verses 36 to 40

The verses as the commentary quotes them
So We subjected to him the wind, blowing by his command, gently, wherever he directed (36) And the devils, every builder and diver (37) And others bound together in shackles (38) This is Our gift, so grant or withhold, without account (39) And indeed, for him with Us is nearness and a good place of return (40)
فَسَخَّرْنا لَهُ الرِّيحَ تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ رُخاءً حَيْثُ أَصابَ (36) وَالشَّياطِينَ كُلَّ بَنَّاءٍ وَغَوَّاصٍ (37) وَآخَرِينَ مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي الْأَصْفادِ (38) هذا عَطاؤُنا فَامْنُنْ أَوْ أَمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ (39) وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنا لَزُلْفى وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ (40)
Vol. 4, p. 95
Both "al-rih" and "al-riyah" have been read. "Rukha'an": gentle, pleasant, not shaking. It is also said: obedient to him, not refusing him. "Haythu asaba": where he aimed and wanted. Al-Asma'i related from the Arabs: "He hit the right (asaba al-sawab) but missed the answer." From
قرئ: الريح، والرياح رُخاءً لينة طيبة لا تزعزع. وقيل: طيعة له لا تمتنع عليه حَيْثُ أَصابَ حيث قصد وأراد. حكى الأصمعى عن العرب: أصاب الصواب فأخطأ الجواب. وعن
Vol. 4, p. 96
Ru'ba: that two men of the people of language sought him out to ask him about this word, so he came out to them and said: "Where are you aiming (ayna tusibani)?" They said: "This is our request," and returned. And it is said: "asaba Allahu bika khayran." "And the devils": conjoined to the wind. "Every builder": a substitute for the devils. "And others": conjoined to "every," entering into the ruling of substitution, and it is a substitution of the whole for the whole: they built for him whatever he wished of buildings, and dived for him and brought out pearls, and he was the first to extract pearls from the sea; and he used to bind the rebellious devils together, some with others, in fetters and chains, for discipline and restraint from corruption. From al-Suddi: he used to gather their hands to their necks, fettered in neck-irons «1». "Al-safad" is the fetter, and the gift was named by it because it is a binding of the one given to. From it is the saying of Ali ؓ: "Whoever does you good has taken you captive, and whoever treats you harshly has set you free." From it too is the saying of one: "Fetter the hands of the one who releases it, and enslave the neck of the one who frees it." And Habib said: "Indeed gift is captivity," and the one who said followed him: "And whoever finds benefaction a fetter is fettered" «2». And they distinguished between the two verbs, saying: "safadahu" means he fettered him, and "asfadahu" means he gave him, like "wa'adahu" and "aw'adahu." That is: this which We gave you of kingdom, wealth and abundance is "Our gift without account," meaning: plentiful, hardly able to be counted and enumerated; "so grant," from "al-minna," which is giving, that is: so give of it what you wish, "or withhold," the disposal of it being entrusted to you. In Ibn Mas'ud's reading: "This, so grant or withhold, is our gift without account"; or: this subjection is Our gift, so grant to whom you wish among the devils release, and withhold whom you wish of them in bonds, without account, that is, there is no reckoning upon you in that.
رؤبة أنّ رجلين من أهل اللغة قصداه ليسألاه عن هذه الكلمة، فخرج إليهما فقال: أين تصيبان؟ فقالا: هذه طلبتنا ورجعا، ويقال: أصاب الله بك خيرا وَالشَّياطِينَ عطف على الريح كُلَّ بَنَّاءٍ بدل من الشياطين وَآخَرِينَ عطف على كل داخل في حكم البدل، وهو بدل الكل من الكل: كانوا يبنون له ما شاء من الأبنية، ويغوصون له فيستخرجون اللؤلؤ، وهو أوّل من استخرج الدرّ من البحر، وكان يقرّن مردة الشياطين بعضهم مع بعض في القيود والسلاسل للتأديب والكف عن الفساد. وعن السدى: كان يجمع أيديهم إلى أعناقهم مغللين في الجوامع «1» . والصفد القيد، وسمى به العطاء لأنه ارتباط للمنعم عليه. ومنه قول علىّ رضى الله عنه: من برّك فقد أسرك، ومن جفاك فقد أطلقك. ومنه قول القائل: غل يدا مطلقها، وأرقّ رقبة معتقها. وقال حبيب: إنّ العطاء إسار، وتبعه من قال: ومن وجد الإحسان قيدا تقيّدا «2» وفرقوا بين الفعلين فقالوا: صفده قيده، وأصفده أعطاه، كوعده وأوعده، أى هذا الذي أعطيناك من الملك والمال والبسطة عَطاؤُنا بغير حساب، يعنى: جما كثيرا لا يكاد يقدر على حسبه وحصره فَامْنُنْ من المنة وهي العطاء، أى: فأعط منه ما شئت أَوْ أَمْسِكْ مفوّضا إليك التصرف فيه. وفي قراءة ابن مسعود: هذا فامنن أو أمسك عطاؤنا بغير حساب، أو هذا التسخير عطاؤنا، فامنن على من شئت من الشياطين بالإطلاق، وأمسك من شئت منهم في الوثاق بغير حساب، أى لا حساب عليك في ذلك.

1. (1) . His statement "in the neck-irons (al-jawami')": in al-Sihah: "al-jami'a" is the neck-iron (al-ghull), because it gathers the two hands to the neck. (Ayn)
2. . "Wa-quyyidtu nafsi fi dhaka mahabbatan / wa-man wajada al-ihsana qaydan taqayyada" by al-Mutanabbi. He says: I left night travel behind my back, that is: I was extreme in leaving it for one who has little wealth, because he never ceases seeking it, and I was satisfied with your great favor; and he likened the hopes that stretched toward him and reached their aims to horses shod with gold, by explicit metaphor, with shoeing as embellishment. It is possible that that is a metonym for the greatness of the favor, and he borrowed fettering for being kept from looking toward anyone other than the one praised and confining praise to him. It is also possible that he likened himself to an animal, with fettering as the imaginative element. "Al-dhara" — with fatha — is whatever covers a thing; one says: "I am in the shade of the mountain and in its dhara," or "in the shade of so-and-so and in his dhara," that is, in his protection and shelter; "mahabbatan" is an object of purpose; and he likened benefaction to a fetter because it is a cause of the self's being owned.
1. (1) . قوله «في الجوامع» في الصحاح «الجامعة» : الغل، لأنها تجمع اليدين إلى العنق. (ع)
2. . وقيدت نفسي في ذراك محبة
…. ومن وجد الإحسان قيدا تقيدا للمتنبي، يقول: تركت سير الليل وراء ظهري، أى: بالغت في تركه لمن قل ماله، لأنه لا زال يبتغيه، واكتفيت بنعمتك العظمى، وشبه الآمال التي امتدت إليه وبلغت مناها، بأفراس منعلة بالذهب على طريق التصريحية والانعال ترشيح. ويجوز أن ذلك كناية عن عظم النعمة، واستعار التقييد للمنع عن التطلع لغير الممدوح وقصر المدح عليه. ويجوز أنه شبه نفسه بحيوان، والتقييد: تخييل. والذرا- بالفتح-: كل ما ستر الشيء، يقال: أنا في ظل الجبل وفي ذراه، أو في ظل فلان وفي ذراه، أى: في كنفه وحماه، ومحبة: مفعول لأجله، وشبه الإحسان بالقيد لأنه سبب استملاك النفس.
21
Q 38:41–44 · Vol. 4, pp. 96–99

Verses 41 to 44

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And remember Our servant Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment" (41) [He was told], "Strike [the ground] with your foot; this is a cool bath and drink" (42) And We granted him his family and the like thereof with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding (43) [And We said], "And take in your hand a bunch of grass and strike with it and do not break your oath." Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning back [to God] (44)
وَاذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا أَيُّوبَ إِذْ نادى رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الشَّيْطانُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذابٍ (41) ارْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ هذا مُغْتَسَلٌ بارِدٌ وَشَرابٌ (42) وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ أَهْلَهُ وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً مِنَّا وَذِكْرى لِأُولِي الْأَلْبابِ (43) وَخُذْ بِيَدِكَ ضِغْثاً فَاضْرِبْ بِهِ وَلا تَحْنَثْ إِنَّا وَجَدْناهُ صابِراً نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ (44)
Vol. 4, p. 97
"Job" is an explicative apposition. And "when (idh)" is a substitute of inclusion from it. "That Satan has touched me": "that he has touched me" is a quotation of his speech in whose cause he called; and had it not been quoted, he would have said "that he touched him," because he is absent. "Bi-nusb" has been read with damma on the nun, and with fatha, with sukun on the sad, and with fatha on both, and with damma on both: "nusb" and "nasb" are like "rushd" and "rashd"; "nasab" is on the original form of the verbal noun, and "nusub" is the heavier form of "nusb"; the meaning is one: fatigue and hardship. And "al-'adhab" is pain; he means his illness and what he endured in it of kinds of suffering «1». It is also said: harm in the body, and torment in the loss of family and property.
أَيُّوبَ عطف بيان. وإِذْ بدل اشتمال منه أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ بأنى مسنى: حكاية لكلامه الذي ناداه بسببه، ولو لم يحك لقال بأنه مسه: لأنه غائب. وقرئ بِنُصْبٍ بضم النون وفتحها مع سكون الصاد، وبفتحهما، وضمهما، فالنصب والنصب: كالرشد والرشد، والنصب: على أصل المصدر، والنصب: تثقيل نصب، والمعنى واحد، وهو التعب والمشقة. والعذاب: الألم، يريد مرضه وما كان يقاسى فيه من أنواع الوصب «1» . وقيل: الضرّ في البدن، والعذاب في ذهاب الأهل والمال
Question
If you say: Why did he ascribe it to Satan, when it is not permissible that God give him power over His prophets to satisfy, by wearying and tormenting them, his need, and had he the ability to do that he would have left no righteous one without afflicting and destroying him, while it has been repeated in the Qur'an that he has no authority but whispering alone?
فإن قلت: لم نسبه إلى الشيطان، ولا يجوز أن يسلطه الله على أنبيائه ليقضى من إتعابهم وتعذيبهم وطره، ولو قدر على ذلك لم يدع صالحا إلا وقد نكبه وأهلكه، وقد تكرّر في القرآن أنه لا سلطان له إلا الوسوسة فحسب؟
Answer
I say: since his whispering to him and his obeying him in what he whispered was a cause of what God afflicted him with of hardship and torment, he ascribed it to him, and he observed courtesy in that, in that he did not ascribe it to God in his supplication, though He is its doer and none but He is able to do it. It is also said: he meant what he used to whisper to him in his illness of magnifying the affliction that had befallen him, and tempting him to dislike and impatience, so he sought refuge in God Most High that He suffice him against that by removing the affliction, or by granting success in repelling and rejecting it with fine patience. It is reported that three of the believers used to visit him, and one of them apostatized, so he asked about him and was told: Satan cast to him that God does not afflict prophets and the righteous. And it is mentioned of the cause of his affliction that a man sought his help against a wrongdoer and he did not help him. It is said: his livestock were in the territory of a disbelieving king, so he flattered him and did not raid him. It is said: he was impressed with the abundance of his wealth. "Strike with your foot": a quotation of what Job was answered with, that is: strike the ground with your foot. From Qatada: it is the land of al-Jabiya «2», so he struck it and a spring gushed, and it was said "this is a cool bath and drink," that is: this is water to wash in and drink from, so your inside and outside will be cured, and you will turn, with no ailment (qalba) in you «3». It is said: two springs gushed for him, so he washed from one and drank from the other, and the illness left his outside and inside by God's leave. It is said: he struck with his right foot and a hot spring gushed, so he washed in it, then with the left and a cold one gushed, so he drank from it. "Mercy from Us and a reminder": both are objects of purpose. The meaning: the gift was for mercy to him and for reminding those of understanding, because when they hear of what
قلت: لما كانت وسوسته إليه وطاعته له فيما وسوس سببا فيما مسه الله به من النصب والعذاب، نسبه إليه، وقد راعى الأدب في ذلك حيث لم ينسبه إلى الله في دعائه، مع أنه فاعله ولا يقدر عليه إلا هو. وقيل: أراد ما كان يوسوس به إليه في مرضه من تعظيم ما نزل به من البلاء، ويغريه على الكراهة والجزع، فالتجأ إلى الله تعالى في أن يكفيه ذلك بكشف البلاء، أو بالتوفيق في دفعه ورده بالصبر الجميل. وروى أنه كان يعوده ثلاثة من المؤمنين، فارتدّ أحدهم، فسأل عنه فقيل ألقى إليه الشيطان: إن الله لا يبتلى الأنبياء والصالحين، وذكر في سبب بلائه أنّ رجلا استغاثه على ظالم فلم يغثه. وقيل: كانت مواشيه في ناحية ملك كافر، فداهنه ولم يغزه. وقيل: أعجب بكثرة ماله ارْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ حكاية ما أجيب به أيوب، أى: اضرب برجلك الأرض. وعن قتادة: هي أرض الجابية «2» فضربها، فنبعت عين فقيل هذا مُغْتَسَلٌ بارِدٌ وَشَرابٌ أى هذا ماء تغتسل به وتشرب منه، فيبرأ باطنك وظاهرك، وتنقلب مآبك قلبة «3» . وقيل: نبعت له عينان، فاغتسل من إحداهما وشرب من الأخرى، فذهب الداء من ظاهره وباطنه بإذن الله، وقيل: ضرب برجله اليمنى فنبعت عين حارة فاغتسل منها، ثم باليسرى فنبعت باردة فشرب منها رَحْمَةً مِنَّا وَذِكْرى مفعول لهما. والمعنى: أنّ الهبة كانت للرحمة له ولتذكير أولى الألباب، لأنهم إذا سمعوا بما
Vol. 4, p. 98
We favored him with because of his patience, it made them desire patience in affliction and the outcome of the patient and what God does for them. "And take": conjoined to "strike." "Al-dighth" is a small bundle of grass or basil or other. From Ibn Abbas: a handful of branches. He had sworn in his illness to strike his wife a hundred [strokes] if he recovered, so God absolved his oath with the easiest thing for him and for her, because of her good service to him and his being pleased with her, and this concession remains. From the Prophet ﷺ: that there was brought to him a deformed man «1» who had behaved lewdly with a slave woman, so he said: "Take a palm cluster containing a hundred twigs and strike him with it one stroke." «2» And it is necessary that the one struck be touched by each one of the hundred, either their tips upright or their breadth spread out, with the form of striking present. The cause of his oath was that she was slow to return to him, having gone on an errand, so his breast was strained. It is also said: she sold her two locks for two loaves, and they were what Job held on to when he stood. It is also said: Satan said to her: Prostrate to me once and I will return to you your property and children, so she intended that but was overtaken by protection; so she mentioned that to him, and he swore. It is also said: Satan made her imagine that Job, if he drank wine, would be cured, so she hinted that to him. It is also said: she asked him to offer a kid to Satan. "We found him patient": We knew him to be patient.
أنعمنا به عليه لصبره، رغبهم في الصبر على البلاء وعاقبة الصابرين وما يفعل الله بهم وَخُذْ معطوف على اركض. والضغث: الحزمة الصغيرة من حشيش أو ريحان أو غير ذلك. وعن ابن عباس: قبضة من الشجر، كان حلف في مرضه ليضربنّ امرأته مائة إذا برأ، فحلل الله يمينه بأهون شيء عليه وعليها لحسن خدمتها إياه ورضاه عنها، وهذه الرخصة باقية. وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنه أتى بمخدج «1» قد خبث بأمة، فقال: «خذوا عثكالا فيه مائة شمراخ فاضربوه بها ضربة» «2» ويجب أن يصيب المضروب كل واحد من المائة، إمّا أطرافها قائمة، وإما أعراضها مبسوطة مع وجود صورة الضرب، وكان السبب في يمينه أنها أبطأت عليه ذاهبة في حاجة فحرج صدره، وقيل: باعت ذؤابتيها برغيفين وكانتا متعلق أيوب إذا قام. وقيل: قال لها الشيطان اسجدي لي سجدة فأردّ عليكم ما لكم وأولادكم، فهمت بذلك فأدركتها العصمة، فذكرت ذلك له، فحلف. وقيل: أوهمها الشيطان أن أيوب إذا شرب الخمر برأ، فعرضت له بذلك. وقيل: سألته أن يقرب للشيطان بعناق وَجَدْناهُ صابِراً علمناه صابرا.
Question
If you say: How did He find him patient when he complained to Him of what afflicted him and asked for His mercy?
فإن قلت: كيف وجده صابرا وقد شكا إليه ما به واسترحمه؟
Answer
I say: Complaint to God, the Mighty and Exalted, is not called impatience, and Jacob ﷺ said: "I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God"; and likewise the sick person's complaint to the physician; for the most patient of people in affliction is not free of wishing for and seeking well-being; so if it is sound to call him patient with wishing for well-being and seeking cure, then let him be called patient with taking refuge in God Most High, and supplication for removal of what ails him, and with seeking treatment and consulting physicians; besides that, Job ﷺ sought healing out of fear for his people of temptation, since Satan was whispering to them as he whispered to him that if he were a prophet he would not have been afflicted with the like of what he was afflicted with, and out of desire for strength for obedience, for his affair had reached the point that nothing remained of him but the heart and the tongue. It is reported that he said in his intimate prayer: "My God, You know that my tongue never opposed my heart, and my heart never followed my sight, and what my right hand possessed never moved me «3», and I never ate except with an orphan with me, and never spent the night satiated or clothed with a hungry or naked person with me," so God removed it from him.
قلت: الشكوى إلى الله عز وعلا لا تسمى جزعا، ولقد قال يعقوب عليه السلام: نَّما أَشْكُوا بَثِّي وَحُزْنِي إِلَى اللَّهِ وكذلك شكوى العليل إلى الطبيب، وذلك أن أصبر الناس على البلاء لا يخلو من تمنى العافية وطلبها، فإذا صحّ أن يسمى صابرا مع تمنى العافية وطلب الشفاء، فليسم صابرا مع اللجإ إلى الله تعالى، والدعاء بكشف ما به ومع التعالج ومشاورة الأطباء، على أن أيوب عليه السلام كان يطلب الشفاء خيفة على قومه من الفتنة. حيث كان الشيطان بوسوس إليهم كما كان يوسوس اليه أنه لو كان نبيا لما ابتلى بمثل ما ابتلى به، وإرادة القوة على الطاعة، فقد بلغ أمره إلى أن لم يبق منه إلا القلب واللسان. ويروى أنه قال في مناجاته: إلهى قد علمت أنه لم يخالف لساني قلبي، ولم يتبع قلبي بصرى، ولم يهبني ما ملكت يمينى، «3» ولم آكل إلا ومعى يتيم، ولم أبت شبعان ولا كاسيا ومعى جائع أو عريان، فكشف الله عنه.
Vol. 4, p. 99

Vol. 4, p. 97
1. (1) . His statement "of kinds of suffering (al-wasab)": in al-Sihah: "al-wasab" is illness. (Ayn)
2. . His statement "it is the land of al-Jabiya": a city in Syria, as in al-Sihah. (Ayn)
3. . His statement "and you will turn, with no ailment (qalba) in you": in al-Sihah: "al-qulab" is a disease that afflicts the camel. And their saying "ma bihi qalba" means: he has no ailment. (Ayn)
1. (1) . قوله «من أنواع الوصب» في الصحاح «الوصب» : المرض. (ع)
2. . قوله «هي أرض الجابية» مدينة بالشام كما في الصحاح. (ع)
3. . قوله «وتنقلب ما بك قلبة» في الصحاح «القلاب» داء يأخذ البعير. وقولهم: ما به قلبة، أى: ليست به علة. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 98
1. (1) . His statement "that he was brought a deformed man (mukhdaj)": "al-khidaj" is deficiency, and "akhdajat al-naqa" is when the she-camel brings forth her young deficient in creation; even if its days were complete, she is a "mukhdij" and the young is a "mukhdaj"; thus in al-Sihah. (Ayn)
2. . Narrated by al-Nasa'i, Ahmad, Ishaq, Ibn Abi Shayba, al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani from the narration of Abu Umama ibn Sahl from Sa'd ibn Ubada. He said: "Among our houses was a weak, deformed man, and the tribe were startled only to find him with one of their slave girls, behaving lewdly with her — the hadith." Al-Bazzar said: nothing else is narrated but this, and its chain is disputed. It was said thus; and it was said: from Abu al-Zinad from Abu Umama, mursal; and Abu Dawud narrated it from another route from Abu Umama, that some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ told him.
3. . His statement "and what my right hand possessed never moved me (yahibni)": that is, did not stir me or excite me, from "habbat al-rih" when it stirred, and "habba al-ba'ir" when it became lively, as in al-Sihah. (Ayn)
1. (1) . قوله «إنه أتى بمخدج» الخداج: النقصان، وأخدجت الناقة: إذا جاءت بولدها ناقص الخلق، وإن كانت أيامه تامة فهي مخدج، والولد مخدج، كذا في الصحاح. (ع)
2. . أخرجه النسائي وأحمد وإسحاق وابن أبى شيبة والبزار والطبراني من رواية أبى أمامة بن سهل عن سعيد بن عبادة. قال «كان بين أبياتنا رجل ضعيف مخدج، فلم يرع الحي إلا وهو على أمة من إمائهم يخبث بها- الحديث» قال البزار: لم يرد إلا هذا، واختلف في إسناده. فقيل هكذا. وقيل عن أبى الزناد عن أبى أمامة مرسلا ورواه أبو داود من وجه آخر عن أبى أمامة أنه أخبره بعض أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.
3. . قوله «ولم يهبني ما ملكت يميني» أى لم ينشطنى ولم يهيجني، من هبت الريح: أى هاجت، وهب البعير: أى نشط، كما في الصحاح. (ع)

Q 38:38–47 · Vol. 4, p. 99

Verses 38 to 47

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And others bound together in shackles (38) This is Our gift, so grant or withhold, without account (39) And indeed, for him with Us is nearness and a good place of return (40) And remember Our servant Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment" (41) [He was told], "Strike [the ground] with your foot; this is a cool bath and drink" (42) And We granted him his family and the like thereof with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding (43) [And We said], "And take in your hand a bunch of grass and strike with it and do not break your oath." Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning back [to God] (44) And remember Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, those of strength and [religious] vision (45) Indeed, We chose them for an exclusive quality: remembrance of the Home [of the Hereafter] (46) And indeed they are, to Us, among the chosen and outstanding (47)
وَآخَرِينَ مُقَرَّنِينَ فِي الْأَصْفادِ (38) هذا عَطاؤُنا فَامْنُنْ أَوْ أَمْسِكْ بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ (39) وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنا لَزُلْفى وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ (40) وَاذْكُرْ عَبْدَنا أَيُّوبَ إِذْ نادى رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الشَّيْطانُ بِنُصْبٍ وَعَذابٍ (41) ارْكُضْ بِرِجْلِكَ هذا مُغْتَسَلٌ بارِدٌ وَشَرابٌ (42) وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ أَهْلَهُ وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً مِنَّا وَذِكْرى لِأُولِي الْأَلْبابِ (43) وَخُذْ بِيَدِكَ ضِغْثاً فَاضْرِبْ بِهِ وَلا تَحْنَثْ إِنَّا وَجَدْناهُ صابِراً نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ (44) وَاذْكُرْ عِبادَنا إِبْراهِيمَ وَإِسْحاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ أُولِي الْأَيْدِي وَالْأَبْصارِ (45) إِنَّا أَخْلَصْناهُمْ بِخالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ (46) وَإِنَّهُمْ عِنْدَنا لَمِنَ الْمُصْطَفَيْنَ الْأَخْيارِ (47)
Vol. 4, p. 99
"Abraham, Isaac and Jacob" is an explicative apposition to "Our servants." And whoever read "Our servant" made Abraham alone the explicative apposition to it, then conjoined his descendants to "Our servant," who are Isaac and Jacob, like the reading of Ibn Abbas: "and the God of your fathers Abraham, Ishmael and Isaac." Since most actions are done with the hands, the word came to predominate, so it was said of every action, "this is of what their hands did," even if it is an action in which hands cannot be involved, or the workers were amputees without hands; and according to that came His saying "those of the hands and the eyes (al-aydi wal-absar)," meaning: those of actions and thought, as though those who do not do the works of the Hereafter, do not strive in God, do not think the thoughts of the people of religions, and have no insight, are in the ruling of the crippled who cannot do the works of their limbs and the deprived of intellects who have no insight. In it is a hint at everyone who was not among God's workers nor among those with insight in God's religion, and a reproach for their leaving striving and contemplation while being capable of both. It has been read "uli al-ayadi" as a plural of a plural. And in Ibn Mas'ud's reading "uli al-ayd," with the ya' dropped and content with the kasra. And explaining it by "al-ayd," from "ta'yid" (support), is unsettled, not firm. "We made them exclusive (akhlasnahum)": We made them pure; "bi-khalisa": by a pure quality with no admixture in it; then He explained it by "remembrance of the Home," as a testimony for the remembrance of the Home to its purity and clarity and the absence of murkiness from it. It has been read in annexation ["by the purity of the remembrance of the Home"]. The meaning: by what is purified of the remembrance of the Home, in that they do not mix the remembrance of the Home with any other concern; their concern is only the remembrance of the Home and nothing else. The meaning of "remembrance of the Home": their remembering the Hereafter constantly, and their forgetting, because of it, the mention of this world; or their reminding of the Hereafter and encouraging toward it and making this world seem small, as is the way of the prophets and their habit. It is said: "remembrance of the Home" is fine praise in this world and the tongue of truth that others do not have.
إِبْراهِيمَ وَإِسْحاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ عطف بيان لعبادنا. ومن قرأ: عبدنا، جعل إبراهيم وحده عطف بيان له، ثم عطف ذريته على عبدنا، وهي إسحاق ويعقوب، كقراءة ابن عباس: وإله أبيك إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق. لما كانت أكثر الأعمال تباشر بالأيدى غلبت، فقيل في كل عمل هذا مما عملت أيديهم، وإن كان عملا لا يتأتى فيه المباشرة بالأيدى. أو كان العمال جذما لا أيدي لهم، وعلى ذلك ورد قوله عز وعلا أُولِي الْأَيْدِي وَالْأَبْصارِ يريد: أولى الأعمال والفكر، كأن الذين لا يعملون أعمال الآخرة، ولا يجاهدون في الله، ولا يفكرون أفكار ذوى الديانات ولا يستبصرون في حكم الزمنى الذين لا يقدرون على أعمال جوارحهم والمسلوبى العقول الذين لا استبصار بهم. وفيه تعريض بكل من لم يكن من عمال الله، ولا من المستبصرين في دين الله، وتوبيخ على تركهم المجاهدة والتأمل مع كونهم متمكنين منهما. وقرئ: أولى الأيادى، على جمع الجمع. وفي قراءة ابن مسعود: أولى الأيد، على طرح الياء والاكتفاء بالكسرة. وتفسيره بالأيد- من التأييد-: قلق غير متمكن أَخْلَصْناهُمْ جعلناهم خالصين بِخالِصَةٍ بخصلة خالصة لا شوب فيها، ثم فسرها بذكرى الدار، شهادة لذكرى الدار بالخلوص والصفاء وانتفاء الكدورة عنها. وقرئ على الإضافة. والمعنى: بما خلص من ذكرى الدار، على أنهم لا يشوبون ذكرى الدار بهمّ آخر، إنما همهم ذكرى الدار لا غير. ومعنى ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ: ذكراهم الآخرة دائبا، ونسيانهم اليها ذكر الدنيا. أو تذكيرهم الآخرة وترغيبهم فيها، وتزهيدهم في الدنيا، كما هو شأن الأنبياء وديدنهم. وقيل. ذكرى الدار. الثناء الجميل في الدنيا ولسان الصدق الذي ليس لغيرهم.
Question
If you say: What is the meaning of "We made them exclusive by an exclusive quality"?
فإن قلت: ما معنى أَخْلَصْناهُمْ بِخالِصَةٍ؟
Answer
I say: its meaning: We made them exclusive because of this quality and because they are among its people; or We made them exclusive by their being granted success for it and kindness to them in choosing it. The first is supported by the reading of one who read "bi-khalisatihim." "Al-mustafayn": the chosen from among their kind. And "al-akhyar" is the plural of "khayr" or "khayyir" lightened, like "al-amwat" as plural of "mayt" or "mayyit."
قلت: معناه: أخلصناهم بسبب هذه الخصلة، وبأنهم من أهلها. أو أخلصناهم بتوفيقهم لها، واللطف بهم في اختيارها. وتعضد الأوّل قراءة من قرأ: بخالصتهم الْمُصْطَفَيْنَ المختارين من أبناء جنسهم. والْأَخْيارِ جمع خير، أو خير، على التخفيف، كالأموات في جمع ميت أو ميت.

Q 38:48 · Vol. 4, pp. 99–100

Verse 48

The verse as the commentary quotes it
And remember Ishmael and Elisha and Dhul-Kifl, and all are among the outstanding (48)
وَاذْكُرْ إِسْماعِيلَ وَالْيَسَعَ وَذَا الْكِفْلِ وَكُلٌّ مِنَ الْأَخْيارِ (48)
Vol. 4, p. 99
"Al-Yasa'": as if the particle of definiteness had entered upon "Yasa'." It has been read "wa-al-Laysa'," as if the particle of definiteness
وَالْيَسَعَ كأن حرف التعريف دخل على يسع. وقرئ: والليسع، كأن حرف التعريف
Vol. 4, p. 100
had entered upon "Laysa'," a "fay'il" form from "al-las'" (stinging). And the tanwin in "wa-kullun" is a substitute for the annexed-to; its meaning: "and all of them are among the outstanding."
دخل على ليسع، فيعل من اللسع. والتنوين في وَكُلٌّ عوض من المضاف اليه، معناه: وكلهم من الأخيار.

1. (1) . Mahmud said: "He only said 'This is a reminder' in order to follow it with another reminder, which is the mention of Paradise and its people, as al-Jahiz says in his books: 'This is a chapter,' then begins another chapter." Ahmad said: And as the jurist says when he mentions the proofs of a question, at the completion of the first proof: "this is a second proof, such and such," to the end of what is in his mind; and the proof of it is that at the end of the mention of the people of Paradise He said: "This! And indeed for the transgressors is an evil place of return," and mentioned the people of the Fire.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «إنما قال: هذا ذكر ليذكر عقبه ذكرا آخر، وهو ذكر الجنة وأهلها، كما يقول الجاحظ في كتبه: فهذا باب، ثم يشرع في باب آخر» قال أحمد: وكما ما يقول الفقيه إذا ذكر أدلة المسألة عند تمام الدليل الأول: هذا دليل ثان كذا وكذا إلى آخر ما في نفسه، ويدل عليه أنه عند انقضاء ذكر أهل الجنة قال: هذا وَإِنَّ لِلطَّاغِينَ لَشَرَّ مَآبٍ فذكر أهل النار.

Q 38:49–52 · Vol. 4, p. 100

Verses 49 to 52

The verses as the commentary quotes them
This is a reminder. And indeed for the righteous is a good place of return (49) Gardens of Eden, whose gates are opened for them (50) Reclining therein, they call therein for abundant fruit and drink (51) And with them are women of restricted glance, of equal age (52)
هذا ذِكْرٌ وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ (49) جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ مُفَتَّحَةً لَهُمُ الْأَبْوابُ (50) مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيها يَدْعُونَ فِيها بِفاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ وَشَرابٍ (51) وَعِنْدَهُمْ قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ أَتْرابٌ (52)
Vol. 4, p. 100
"This is a reminder": that is, this is a kind of reminder, which is the Qur'an, since when He had run the mention of the prophets and completed it, and it is a chapter of the chapters of revelation and a kind of its kinds, and He wanted to mention after it another chapter, which is the mention of Paradise and its people «1», He said "this is a reminder," then said "and indeed for the righteous," as al-Jahiz says in his books: "this is a chapter," then he begins another chapter; and as the scribe says when he has finished a section of his book and wants to begin another: "This, and it was such and such"; the proof of it is that when He finished the mention of the people of Paradise and wanted to follow it with the mention of the people of the Fire, He said: "This! And indeed for the transgressors." It is also said: its meaning: this is an honor and a fine remembrance by which they will be remembered forever. From Ibn Abbas ؓ: this is the remembrance of the prophets who passed. "Gardens of Eden": definite, because of His saying "the Gardens of Eden which the Most Merciful has promised," and its accusative is as an explicative apposition to "good place of return." And "mufattahatan" is a circumstantial clause, and the operator in it is what is in "for the righteous" of the meaning of the verb. And in "mufattahatan" is a pronoun of the gardens. And "al-abwab" is a substitute for the pronoun, its estimation being: "opened, the gates," like their saying: "Zayd struck the hand and the foot," and it is a substitution of inclusion. It has been read "jannatu 'adnin mufattahatun" in the nominative, on the basis that "jannatu 'adnin" is a subject and "mufattahatun" its predicate; or both are predicates of an omitted subject, that is: "it is gardens of Eden, they are opened for them." "Atrab": as if peers were called "atrab" because the soil (turab) touched them at one time; and they were made of one age because affection among equals is firmer. It is also said: they are peers for their husbands, their ages like their ages.
هذا ذِكْرٌ أى: هذا نوع من الذكر وهو القرآن، لما أجرى ذكر الأنبياء وأتمه، وهو باب من أبواب التنزيل، ونوع من أنواعه، وأراد أن يذكر على عقبه بابا آخر، وهو ذكر الجنة وأهلها، «1» قال: هذا ذكر، ثم قال وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ كما يقول الجاحظ في كتبه: فهذا باب، ثم يشرع في باب آخر، ويقول الكاتب إذا فرغ من فصل من كتابه وأراد الشروع في آخر: هذا وقد كان كيت وكيت، والدليل عليه: أنه لما أتم ذكر أهل الجنة وأراد أن يعقبه بذكر أهل النار. قال: هذا وإن للطاغين. وقيل: معناه هذا شرف وذكر جميل يذكرون به أبدا. وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنه: هذا ذكر من مضى من الأنبياء جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ معرفة لقوله جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ الَّتِي وَعَدَ الرَّحْمنُ وانتصابها على أنها عطف بيان لحسن مآب. ومُفَتَّحَةً حال، والعامل فيها ما في لِلْمُتَّقِينَ من معنى الفعل. وفي مُفَتَّحَةً ضمير الجنات. والأبواب بدل من الضمير، تقديره: مفتحة هي الأبواب، كقولهم: ضرب زيد اليد والرجل، وهو من بدل الاشتمال. وقرئ: جنات عدن مفتحة، بالرفع، على أن جنات عدن مبتدأ، ومفتحة خبره. أو كلاهما خبر مبتدإ محذوف، أى: هو جنات عدن هي مفتحة لهم، كأن اللدات سمين أترابا، لأن التراب مسهن في وقت واحد، وانما جعلن على سنّ واحدة، لأن التحاب بين الأقران أثبت. وقيل: هنّ أتراب لأزواجهن، أسنانهنّ كأسنانهم:

Q 38:53–54 · Vol. 4, pp. 100–101

Verses 53 to 54

The verses as the commentary quotes them
This is what you are promised for the Day of Account (53) Indeed, this is Our provision; for it there is no depletion (54)
هذا ما تُوعَدُونَ لِيَوْمِ الْحِسابِ (53) إِنَّ هذا لَرِزْقُنا ما لَهُ مِنْ نَفادٍ (54)
Vol. 4, p. 100
"Tu'adun" and "yu'adun" have been read, with ta' and ya'. "For the Day of Account": for the sake of the Day of Account, as you say: "This is what you store up for the Day of Account," that is, for the Day when every soul is recompensed for what it did.
قرئ: يوعدون، بالتاء والياء لِيَوْمِ الْحِسابِ لأجل يوم الحساب، كما تقول: هذا ما تدخرونه ليوم الحساب، أى: ليوم تجزى كل نفس ما عملت.

Vol. 4, p. 100
1. (1) . Mahmud said: "He only said 'This is a reminder' in order to follow it with another reminder, which is the mention of Paradise and its people, as al-Jahiz says in his books: 'This is a chapter,' then begins another chapter." Ahmad said: And as the jurist says when he mentions the proofs of a question, at the completion of the first proof: "this is a second proof, such and such," to the end of what is in his mind; and the proof of it is that at the end of the mention of the people of Paradise He said: "This! And indeed for the transgressors is an evil place of return," and mentioned the people of the Fire.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «إنما قال: هذا ذكر ليذكر عقبه ذكرا آخر، وهو ذكر الجنة وأهلها، كما يقول الجاحظ في كتبه: فهذا باب، ثم يشرع في باب آخر» قال أحمد: وكما ما يقول الفقيه إذا ذكر أدلة المسألة عند تمام الدليل الأول: هذا دليل ثان كذا وكذا إلى آخر ما في نفسه، ويدل عليه أنه عند انقضاء ذكر أهل الجنة قال: هذا وَإِنَّ لِلطَّاغِينَ لَشَرَّ مَآبٍ فذكر أهل النار.
Vol. 4, p. 101
1. (1) . His statement "and it has been read 'min shikli-hi' with kasra, and it is a dialect": that is, in "shakl" in the sense of "likeness." (Ayn)
2. . "As for al-ghunj, it is with kasra only": in al-Sihah: "al-ghunj" and "al-ghinj": coquetry (shikl), and "ghanijat al-jariya wa-taghannajat," so she is "ghanija." And in it: "al-shakl" — with fatha — is the likeness, and with kasra is coquetry (al-dall); one says "a woman of shikl." (Ayn)

2. . «وأما الغنج فبالكسر لا غير» في الصحاح: الغنج والغنج: الشكل، وقد غنجت الجارية وتغنجت، فهي غنجة. وفيه: الشكل- بالفتح-: المثل، وبالكسر: الدل، يقال: امرأة ذات شكل. (ع)

Q 38:55–61 · Vol. 4, pp. 101–102

Verses 55 to 61

The verses as the commentary quotes them
This! And indeed for the transgressors is an evil place of return (55) Hell, which they will enter, and wretched is the resting place (56) This! So let them taste it: scalding water and purulence (57) And other [torments] of its like, in pairs (58) "This is a company rushing headlong with you; no welcome for them. Indeed, they will burn in the Fire" (59) They will say, "Rather, you - no welcome for you. You brought it upon us, and wretched is the settlement" (60) They will say, "Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us - increase him in the Fire with double torment" (61)
هذا وَإِنَّ لِلطَّاغِينَ لَشَرَّ مَآبٍ (55) جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَها فَبِئْسَ الْمِهادُ (56) هذا فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ وَغَسَّاقٌ (57) وَآخَرُ مِنْ شَكْلِهِ أَزْواجٌ (58) هذا فَوْجٌ مُقْتَحِمٌ مَعَكُمْ لا مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ إِنَّهُمْ صالُوا النَّارِ (59) قالُوا بَلْ أَنْتُمْ لا مَرْحَباً بِكُمْ أَنْتُمْ قَدَّمْتُمُوهُ لَنا فَبِئْسَ الْقَرارُ (60) قالُوا رَبَّنا مَنْ قَدَّمَ لَنا هذا فَزِدْهُ عَذاباً ضِعْفاً فِي النَّارِ (61)
Vol. 4, p. 101
"This": that is, the matter is this; or: this as mentioned. "Wretched is the resting place": like His saying "They will have a bed of Hell and above them coverings"; He likened what is beneath them of fire to the resting place which a sleeper spreads, that is: this is scalding water, so let them taste it. Or: the torment is this, so let them taste it; then He began and said: it is scalding water and purulence. Or: "this, so let them taste it" is in the position of "and Me, so fear Me," that is: let them taste this, so let them taste it. And "ghassaq" — with lightening and doubling — is what oozes (yaghsiqu) of the pus of the people of the Fire; one says "ghasaqat al-'ayn" when its tears flow. It is also said: the scalding water burns with its heat, and the ghassaq burns with its cold. It is also said: if a drop of it were dripped in the East, the people of the West would stink, and if a drop of it were dripped in the West, the people of the East would stink. From al-Hasan ؓ: the ghassaq is a torment that none knows but God Most High. People concealed obedience for God, so He concealed for them a reward in His saying "So no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes," and they concealed disobedience, so He concealed for them a punishment. "And another": and other tasted things of the kind of this tasted thing, of its like in severity and ghastliness, "azwaj": kinds. It has been read "wa-akhar" [plural], that is: and another torment, or another tasted thing. And "azwaj" is a description of "akhar," because it may be in varieties; or a description of the three, which are scalding water, ghassaq, and another of its kind. It has been read "min shikli-hi" with kasra «1», and it is a dialect. As for "al-ghunj" «2», it is with kasra only. "This is a company rushing headlong with you": this is a dense crowd that has rushed into the Fire with you, that is, entered the Fire in your company and association; and "iqtiham" is riding hardship and entering into it. And "al-qahma" is hardship. And this is a quotation of the speech of the transgressors to one another, that is, they will say this. And what is meant by "the company" is their followers who rushed with them into error, so they rush with them into the torment; "no welcome for them" is a prayer by them against their followers. You say to one for whom you pray: "Marhaban," that is: you came to a spacious land, not a narrow one; or: your land is spacious (rahibat biladuka rahban); then "la" enters upon it in an evil prayer.
هذا أى الأمر هذا: أو هذا كما ذكر فَبِئْسَ الْمِهادُ كقوله لَهُمْ مِنْ جَهَنَّمَ مِهادٌ وَمِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ غَواشٍ شبه ما تحتهم من النار بالمهاد الذي يفترشه النائم، أى: هذا حميم فليذوقوه. أو العذاب هذا فليذوقوه، ثم ابتدأ فقال: هو حَمِيمٌ وَغَسَّاقٌ أو: هذا فليذوقوه بمنزلة وَإِيَّايَ فَارْهَبُونِ أى ليذوقوا هذا فليذوقوه، والغساق- بالتخفيف والتشديد-: ما يغسق من صديد أهل النار، يقال: غسقت العين، إذا سال دمعها. وقيل: الحميم يحرق بحرّه، والغساق يحرق ببرده. وقيل: لو قطرت منه قطرة في المشرق لنتنت أهل المغرب، ولو قطرت منه قطرة في المغرب لنتنت أهل المشرق. وعن الحسن رضى الله عنه. الغساق: عذاب لا يعلمه إلا الله تعالى. إن الناس أخفوا لله طاعة فأخفى لهم ثوابا في قوله فَلا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ ما أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ وأخفوا معصية فأخفى لهم عقوبة وَآخَرُ ومذوقات أخر من شكل هذا المذوق من مثله في الشدة والفظاعة أَزْواجٌ أجناس. وقرئ: وآخر، أى: وعذاب آخر. أو مذوق آخر. وأزواج: صفة لآخر، لأنه يجوز أن يكون ضروبا. أو صفة للثلاثة وهي حميم وغساق وآخر من شكله. وقرئ: من شكله، بالكسر «1» وهي لغة. وأما الغنج «2» فبالكسر لا غير هذا فَوْجٌ مُقْتَحِمٌ مَعَكُمْ هذا جمع كثيف قد اقتحم معكم النار، أى دخل النار في صحبتكم وقرانكم، والاقتحام: ركوب الشدة والدخول فيها. والقحمة: الشدة. وهذه حكاية كلام الطاغين بعضهم مع بعض، أى: يقولون هذا. والمراد بالفوج: أتباعهم الذين اقتحموا معهم الضلالة، فيقتحمون معهم العذاب لا مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ دعاء منهم على أتباعهم. تقول لمن تدعو له: مرحبا، أى: أتيت رحبا من البلاد لا ضيقا: أو رحبت بلادك رحبا، ثم تدخل عليه «لا» في دعاء السوء.
Vol. 4, p. 102
"Bihim" is a clarification of those prayed against. "They will burn in the Fire": a reason for their deserving the prayer against them. Like it is His saying "Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister." It is also said: "This is a company rushing headlong with you" is the speech of the keepers [of Hell] to the chiefs of the disbelievers about their followers, and "no welcome for them; indeed they will burn in the Fire" is the speech of the chiefs. And it is said: all of this is the speech of the keepers. "They said": that is, the followers: "Rather, you — no welcome for you": they mean the prayer you prayed against us, you are more deserving of it, and they gave as the reason their saying "You brought it upon us," and the pronoun is for the torment or for their burning.
وبِهِمْ بيان للمدعو عليهم إِنَّهُمْ صالُوا النَّارِ تعليل لاستيجابهم للدعاء عليهم. ونحوه قوله تعالى كُلَّما دَخَلَتْ أُمَّةٌ لَعَنَتْ أُخْتَها وقيل: هذا فوج مقتحم معكم: كلام الخزنة لرؤساء الكفرة في أتباعهم. ولا مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ إِنَّهُمْ صالُوا النَّارِ كلام الرؤساء. وقيل: هذا كله كلام الخزنة قالُوا أى الأتباع بَلْ أَنْتُمْ لا مَرْحَباً بِكُمْ يريدون الدعاء الذي دعوتم به علينا أنتم أحق به، وعللوا ذلك بقولهم أَنْتُمْ قَدَّمْتُمُوهُ لَنا والضمير للعذاب أو لصلبهم.
Question
If you say: What is the meaning of their having brought the torment forward for them?
فإن قلت: ما معنى تقديمهم العذاب لهم؟
Answer
I say: what is brought forward is evil deeds. God Almighty said "Taste the torment of burning. That is for what your hands have put forth." But when the chiefs were the cause of it by their misleading and the torment was their recompense for it, it was said "you brought it forward for us," making the chiefs the ones who brought it forward and making the recompense the thing brought forward, so He combined two figures, because the doers are in truth the ones who brought forward, not their chiefs, and the deed is what is brought forward, not its recompense.
قلت: المقدم هو عمل السوء. قال الله تعالى ذُوقُوا عَذابَ الْحَرِيقِ ذلِكَ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ ولكن الرؤساء لما كانوا السبب فيه بإغوائهم وكان العذاب جزاءهم عليه: قيل أنتم قدمتموه لنا، فجعل الرؤساء هم المقدمين وجعل الجزاء هو المقدّم، فجمع بين مجازين، لأن العاملين هم المقدمون في الحقيقة لا رؤساؤهم، والعمل هو المقدم لاجزاؤه.
Question
If you say: As for the one who made "no welcome for them" part of the speech of the keepers, what does he do with "Rather, you — no welcome for you," when those addressed — I mean their chiefs — did not speak with anything to which this would be a reply?
فإن قلت: فالذي جعل قوله لا مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ من كلام الخزنة ما يصنع بقوله بَلْ أَنْتُمْ لا مَرْحَباً بِكُمْ والمخاطبون- أعنى رؤساءهم- لم يتكلموا بما يكون هذا جوابا لهم؟
Answer
I say: it is as if it were said: this which the keepers prayed against us, you, O chiefs, are more deserving of it than we, for your misleading us and your being the cause of what we are in of torment; and this is sound, as if a people embellished some evils to a people and they committed them, and it were said to the embellishers: "May God disgrace these, how evil their deed!" so the embellisher says to the embellishers: "Rather, you are more deserving of disgrace than we, for had it not been for you we would not have committed that." "They said": they too, the followers: "so increase him with double torment (di'fan)," that is, doubled, and its meaning: having a double. Like it is His saying "Our Lord, these misled us, so give them double torment," which is that He adds to his torment its like, so it becomes two-fold, as in His saying "Our Lord, give them two-fold of the torment" «1», and it came in the exegesis "double torment": snakes and vipers «2».
قلت: كأنه قيل: هذا الذي دعا به علينا الخزنة أنتم يا رؤساء أحق به منا لإغوائكم إيانا ونسببكم فيما نحن فيه من العذاب، وهذا صحيح كما لو زين قوم لقوم بعض المساوى فارتكبوه فقيل للمزينين: أخزى الله هؤلاء ما أسوأ فعلهم؟ فقال المزين لهم للمزينين: بل أنتم أولى بالخزي منا، فلولا أنتم لم نرتكب ذلك قالُوا هم الأتباع أيضا فَزِدْهُ عَذاباً ضِعْفاً أى مضاعفا، ومعناه: ذا ضعف: ونحوه قوله تعالى رَبَّنا هؤُلاءِ أَضَلُّونا فَآتِهِمْ عَذاباً ضِعْفاً وهو أن يزيد على عذابه مثله فيصير ضعفين، كقوله عز وجل رَبَّنا آتِهِمْ ضِعْفَيْنِ مِنَ الْعَذابِ «1» وجاء في التفسير عَذاباً ضِعْفاً: حيات وأفاعى «2» .

1. (1) . His saying, Exalted: "They will say, 'Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase him with double torment,'" and He said in another place: "Give them two-fold of the torment and curse them with a great curse," and the story is one. Q 38:62–63 · Vol. 4, pp. 102–103

Verses 62 to 63

The verses as the commentary quotes them
And they will say, "What is [wrong] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the worst [of people]? (62) Did we take them in ridicule, or have [our] eyes turned away from them?" (63)
وَقالُوا ما لَنا لا نَرى رِجالاً كُنَّا نَعُدُّهُمْ مِنَ الْأَشْرارِ (62) أَتَّخَذْناهُمْ سِخْرِيًّا أَمْ زاغَتْ عَنْهُمُ الْأَبْصارُ (63)
Vol. 4, p. 102
"And they said": the pronoun is for the transgressors; "men": they mean the poor Muslims who were paid no attention; "among the worst": the lowly in whom is no good or benefit, and because they were on other than their religion, they were evil in their eyes. "Did we take them in ridicule" has been read in the declarative form, as a description of "men," like "we used to count them among the worst"
وَقالُوا الضمير للطاغين رِجالًا يعنون فقراء المسلمين الذين لا يؤبه لهم مِنَ الْأَشْرارِ من الأراذل الذين لا خير فيهم ولا جدوى، ولأنهم كانوا على خلاف دينهم، فكانوا عندهم أشرارا أَتَّخَذْناهُمْ سِخْرِيًّا قرئ بلفظ الإخبار على أنه صفة لرجالا، مثل قوله كُنَّا نَعُدُّهُمْ مِنَ الْأَشْرارِ
Vol. 4, p. 103
and with the interrogative hamza, as a denial against themselves and a rebuke «1» for their ridiculing them. And His saying "or have [our] eyes turned away from them" has two aspects of connection. One: that it connect with "What is [wrong] with us": "what is wrong with us that we do not see them in the Fire? as if they were not in it, or have our eyes turned away from them so we do not see them while they are in it?" They divided their affair between their being of the people of Paradise and their being of the people of the Fire, except that their place was hidden from them. The second aspect: that it connect with "did we take them in ridicule": either "am" is connective, in the sense of "which of the two acts did we do to them: ridicule of them, or disdain and contempt, and our eyes rose above them and overlooked them," in the sense of denying both matters of themselves; from al-Hasan: they did all of it, took them in ridicule and their eyes turned away from them, belittling them. Or "am" is detached after the passing of "did we take them in ridicule" as a report or a question, like your saying: "Are they camels or sheep?" and "Is Zayd with you or is Amr?"; and you may estimate the interrogative hamza omitted for whoever read without its hamza, because "am" indicates it, so the two readings do not differ: the affirming of the interrogative hamza and its omission. It is said: the pronoun in "and they said" is for the chiefs of Quraysh like Abu Jahl and al-Walid and their likes, and the men are Ammar, Suhayb, Bilal and their likes. "Sikhriyyan" has been read with damma and with kasra.
وبهمزة الاستفهام على أنه إنكار على أنفسهم وتأنيب لها «1» في الاستسخار منهم. وقوله أَمْ زاغَتْ عَنْهُمُ الْأَبْصارُ له وجهان من الاتصال، أحدهما: أن يتصل بقوله ما لَنا أى: مالنا لا نراهم في النار؟ كأنهم ليسوا فيها بل أزاغت عنهم أبصارنا فلا نراهم وهم فيها: قسموا أمرهم بين أن يكونوا من أهل الجنة، وبين أن يكونوا من أهل النار. إلا أنه خفى عليهم مكانهم. والوجه الثاني: أن يتصل باتخذناهم سخريا، إما أن تكون أم متصلة على معنى: أى الفعلين فعلنا بهم الاستسخار منهم، أم الازدراء بهم والتحقير، وأن أبصارنا كانت تعلو عنهم وتقتحمهم، على معنى إنكار الأمرين جميعا على أنفسهم، وعن الحسن: كل ذلك قد فعلوا، اتخذوهم سخريا وزاغت عنهم أبصارهم محقرة لهم. وإما أن تكون منقطعة بعد مضى اتخذناهم سخريا على الخبر أو الاستفهام، كقولك: إنها إبل أم شاء، وأزيد عندك أم عندك عمرو: ولك أن تقدّر همزة الاستفهام محذوفة فيمن قرأ بغير همزته، لأنّ «أم» تدل عليها، فلا تفترق القراءتان: إثبات همزة الاستفهام وحذفها. وقيل: الضمير في وَقالُوا لصناديد قريش كأبى جهل والوليد وأضرابهما، والرجال: عمار وصهيب وبلال وأشباههم. وقرئ: سخريا، بالضم والكسر.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 4, p. 102
1. (1) . His saying, Exalted: "They will say, 'Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase him with double torment,'" and He said in another place: "Give them two-fold of the torment and curse them with a great curse," and the story is one. Ahmad said: In it is proof that "di'fayn" is two of one thing, contrary to those who said otherwise, because in one place He said "increase him with double torment," and what is meant is the like of his torment, so they would be two torments; and in two places He said "di'fayn," and what is meant is: possessing two torments. [.....]
2. . His statement "and it came in the exegesis ... etc.": the wording of al-Khazin: Ibn Abbas said: snakes and vipers. (Ayn)
1. (1) . قوله تعالى قالُوا رَبَّنا مَنْ قَدَّمَ لَنا هذا فَزِدْهُ عَذاباً ضِعْفاً وقال في موضع آخر آتِهِمْ ضِعْفَيْنِ مِنَ الْعَذابِ وَالْعَنْهُمْ لَعْناً كَبِيراً والقصة واحدة. قال أحمد: وفيه دليل على أن الضعفين اثنان من شيء واحد، خلافا لمن قال غير ذلك، لأنه في موضع قال فَزِدْهُ عَذاباً ضِعْفاً والمراد: مثل عذابه، فيكونا عذابين. وقال في موضعين ضِعْفَيْنِ والمراد: ذا عذابين. [.....]

…. الخ» عبارة الخازن: قال ابن عباس: حيات وأفاعى (ع)

I say: their exchange of speech and the question and answer that pass between them was likened to what passes between disputants of the like of that, and because the chiefs' saying 'no welcome for them' and their followers' saying 'rather you, no welcome for you' is of the sort of dispute." Ahmad said: This confirms that what preceded of His saying "no welcome for them; indeed they will burn in the Fire" is the speech of the arrogant disbelievers, and His saying "rather you, no welcome for you" is the speech of the followers; so on this interpretation the dispute occurred from both sides, and so quarreling is realized, contrary to whoever said that the first is the speech of the keepers of Hell and the second the speech of the followers, for on that estimation the dispute would be only from one of the two parties; so the first interpretation is more feasible and firmer.
1. (1) . قوله «وتأنيب لها» أى: تعنيف ولوم. أفاده الصحاح. (ع)
2. . قال محمود: «إن قلت لم سمي ذلك تخاصما؟ قلت: شبه تقاولهم وما يجرى بينهم من السؤال والجواب بما يجرى بين المتخاصمين من نحو ذلك، ولأن قول الرؤساء: لا مرحبا بهم، وقول أتباعهم: بل أنتم لا مرحبا بكم، من باب الخصومة» قال أحمد: هذا يحقق أن ما تقدم من قوله لا مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ إِنَّهُمْ صالُوا النَّارِ من قول المتكبرين الكفار، وقوله تعالى بَلْ أَنْتُمْ لا مَرْحَباً بِكُمْ من قول الأتباع، فالخصومة على هذا التأويل حصلت من الجهتين، فيتحقق التخاصم، خلافا لمن قال: إن الأول من كلام خزنة جهنم، والثاني: من كلام الأتباع، فانه على هذا التقدير إنما تكون الخصومة من أحد الفريقين فالتفسير الأول أمكن وأثبت.
28
Q 38:64 · Vol. 4, p. 103

Verse 64

The verse as the commentary quotes it
Indeed, that is truth: the quarreling of the people of the Fire (64)
إِنَّ ذلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخاصُمُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ (64)
Vol. 4, p. 103
"Indeed, that": that is, what we related of them, "is truth": they must speak it; then He explained what it is, so He said: it is "the quarreling of the people of the Fire." It has been read in the accusative as a description of "that," because demonstrative nouns are described by generic nouns.
إِنَّ ذلِكَ أى الذي حكينا عنهم لَحَقٌّ لا بد أن يتكلموا به، ثم بين ما هو فقال هو تَخاصُمُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ وقرئ بالنصب على أنه صفة لذلك، لأن أسماء الإشارة توصف بأسماء الأجناس.
Question
If you say: Why was that called quarreling?
فإن قلت: لم سمى ذلك تخاصما؟
Answer
I say: their exchange of speech and the question and answer that pass between them was likened to what passes between disputants of the like of that «2», and because the chiefs' saying "no welcome for them" and their followers' saying "rather you, no welcome for you" is of the sort of dispute, so the whole exchange was called quarreling because of its including that.
قلت: شبه تقاولهم وما يجرى بينهم من السؤال والجواب بما يجرى بين المتخاصمين من نحو ذلك «2» ولأنّ قول الرؤساء: لا مرحبا بهم، وقول أتباعهم: بل أنتم لا مرحبا بكم، من باب الخصومة، فسمى التقاول كله تخاصما لأجل اشتماله على ذلك.
