Q 38:65–66 · Vol. 4, pp. 103–104

Verses 65 to 66

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Say, "I am only a warner, and there is no god except God, the One, the Prevailing (65) Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving" (66)
قُلْ إِنَّما أَنَا مُنْذِرٌ وَما مِنْ إِلهٍ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ الْواحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ (65) رَبُّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُمَا الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفَّارُ (66)
Vol. 4, p. 104
Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of Makkah: I am only a messenger, a warner; I warn you of God's torment for the polytheists, and I tell you: the religion of truth is the oneness of God, and that one believes that there is no god but God, "the One" without peer or partner, "the Prevailing" over everything, and that dominion and lordship in the whole world are His, and He is "the Exalted in Might," who is not overcome when He punishes the disobedient, and with that He is "the Forgiving" of the sins of whoever takes refuge in Him. Or: say to them: I am only a warner to you as I know; and I warn you of the punishment of One of whom this is the description, for the like of Him is worthy of having His punishment feared as He is worthy of having His reward hoped for.
قُلْ يا محمد لمشركي مكة: ما أنا إلا رسول مُنْذِرٌ أنذركم عذاب الله للمشركين، وأقول لكم: إنّ دين الحق توحيد الله، وأن يعتقد أن لا إله إلا الله الْواحِدُ بلا ندّ ولا شريك الْقَهَّارُ لكل شيء، وأنّ الملك والربوبية له في العالم كله وهو الْعَزِيزُ الذي لا يغلب إذا عاقب العصاة، وهو مع ذلك الْغَفَّارُ لذنوب من التجأ إليه. أو قل لهم ما أنا إلا منذر لكم ما أعلم، وأنا أنذركم عقوبة من هذه صفته، فإنّ مثله حقيق بأن يخاف عقابه كما هو حقيق بأن يرجى ثوابه.

Q 38:67–70 · Vol. 4, pp. 104–105

Verses 67 to 70

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Say, "It is a great news (67) From which you are turning away (68) I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly when they were disputing (69) It is not revealed to me except that I am a clear warner" (70)
قُلْ هُوَ نَبَأٌ عَظِيمٌ (67) أَنْتُمْ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضُونَ (68) ما كانَ لِي مِنْ عِلْمٍ بِالْمَلَإِ الْأَعْلى إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ (69) إِنْ يُوحى إِلَيَّ إِلاَّ أَنَّما أَنَا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ (70)
Vol. 4, p. 104
"Say, it is a great news": that is, this which I have informed you of, my being a warning messenger and that God is One, with no partner, is a great news, from the like of which none turns away but one heedless, extremely heedless. Then He argued for the soundness of his prophethood in that what he informs of regarding the exalted assembly and their disputing is a matter of which he had no knowledge at all, then he knew it, and he did not take the road that people take in knowing what they did not know, which is taking from the people of knowledge and reading books, so it was known that this was not obtained except by revelation from God. "It is not revealed to me except that I am a warner": that is, "because I am a warner." Its meaning: it is revealed to me only for warning, so the lam is omitted and it is accusative by the verb's reaching it. It is also possible that it be nominative, in the sense: it is not revealed to me except this, which is that I warn and convey and do not exceed in that, that is, I am commanded only with this one command alone, and there is nothing for me beyond that. It has been read "innama" with kasra on the basis of quotation, that is: except this saying, which is that I say to you: "I am only a clear warner," and I claim nothing else. It is said: the great news is the stories of Adam ﷺ and informing of it without hearing from anyone. From Ibn Abbas: the Qur'an. From al-Hasan: the Day of Resurrection.
قُلْ هُوَ نَبَأٌ عَظِيمٌ أى هذا الذي أنبأتكم به من كوني رسولا منذرا وأن الله واحد لا شريك له: نبأ عظيم لا يعرض عن مثله إلا غافل شديد الغفلة. ثم احتج لصحة نبوّته بأنّ ما ينبئ به عن الملإ الأعلى واختصامهم أمر ما كان له به من علم قط، ثم علمه ولم يسلك الطريق الذي يسلكه الناس في علم ما لم يعلموا، وهو الأخذ من أهل العلم وقراءة الكتب، فعلم أنّ ذلك لم يحصل إلا بالوحي من الله إِنْ يُوحى إِلَيَّ إِلَّا أَنَّما أَنَا نَذِيرٌ أى لأنما أنا نذير. ومعناه: ما يوحى إلىّ إلا للإنذار، فحذف اللام وانتصب بإفضاء الفعل إليه. ويجوز أن يرتفع على معنى: ما يوحى إلىّ إلا هذا، وهو أن أنذر وأبلغ ولا أفرط في ذلك، أى ما أو مر إلا بهذا الأمر وحده، وليس إلىّ غير ذلك. وقرئ إنما بالكسر على الحكاية، أى: إلا هذا القول، وهو أن أقول لكم: إنما أنا نذير مبين ولا أدعى شيئا آخر. وقيل: النبأ العظيم: قصص آدم عليه السلام والإنباء به من غير سماع من أحد. وعن ابن عباس: القرآن. وعن الحسن: يوم القيامة.
Question
If you say: To what does "when they were disputing" relate?
فإن قلت: بم يتعلق إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ؟
Answer
I say: to an omitted [word], because the meaning is: I had no knowledge of the speech of the exalted assembly at the time of their disputing, and "when He said" is a substitute for "when they were disputing."
قلت: بمحذوف، لأن المعنى: ما كان لي من علم بكلام الملإ الأعلى وقت اختصامهم، وإِذْ قالَ بدل من إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ.
Question
If you say: What is meant by the exalted assembly?
فإن قلت: ما المراد بالملإ الأعلى؟
Answer
I say: the people of the story: the angels, Adam and Iblis, because they were in heaven and the exchange was among them.
قلت: أصحاب القصة الملائكة وآدم وإبليس، لأنهم كانوا في السماء وكان التقاول بينهم:
Question
If you say: The exchange among them was only between God Almighty and them, because God, Glorified and Exalted, is the One who spoke to them and they spoke to Him, so you are between two matters: either you say the exalted assembly is these, and the exchange was among them, yet the exchange was not among them; or you say the exchange was between God and them, so you have made Him part of the exalted assembly.
فإن قلت: ما كان التقاول بينهم إنما كان بين الله تعالى وبينهم، لأن الله سبحانه وتعالى هو الذي قال لهم وقالوا له، فأنت بين أمرين: إما أن تقول الملأ الأعلى هؤلاء، وكان التقاول بينهم ولم يكن التفاؤل بينهم وإما أن تقول: التقاول كان بين الله وبينهم، فقد جعلته من الملإ الأعلى.
Answer
I say: God's speaking was through an angel as intermediary, so the speaker in reality was the intermediary angel, so it was sound that the exchange was
قلت: كانت مقاولة الله سبحانه بواسطة ملك، فكان المقاول في الحقيقة هو الملك المتوسط، فصح أن التقاول كان
Vol. 4, p. 105
between the angels, Adam and Iblis, and they are the exalted assembly. And what is meant by disputing is the exchange, as passed.
بين الملائكة وآدم وإبليس، وهم الملأ الأعلى. والمراد بالاختصام: التقاول على ما سبق.

Vol. 4, p. 104
None
None
Vol. 4, p. 105
1. (1) . His statement "your hands tied (yadaka awkata)": in al-Sihah: "awka 'ala ma fi siqa'ihi," when he tied it with the waterskin-string (wika'). (Ayn)
1. (1) . قوله «يداك أوكتا» في الصحاح: أوكى على ما في سقائه: إذا شده بالوكاء. (ع)
31
Q 38:71–74 · Vol. 4, p. 105

Verses 71 to 74

The verses as the commentary quotes them
[Mention] when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will create a human being from clay (71) So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down to him in prostration" (72) So the angels prostrated, all of them entirely (73) Except Iblis; he was arrogant and became among the disbelievers (74)
إِذْ قالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلائِكَةِ إِنِّي خالِقٌ بَشَراً مِنْ طِينٍ (71) فَإِذا سَوَّيْتُهُ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِي فَقَعُوا لَهُ ساجِدِينَ (72) فَسَجَدَ الْمَلائِكَةُ كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ (73) إِلاَّ إِبْلِيسَ اسْتَكْبَرَ وَكانَ مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ (74)
Vol. 4, p. 105
Question
If you say: How was it sound for Him to say to them "Indeed, I will create a human being" when they did not know what a human being is and had no acquaintance with it before?
فإن قلت: كيف صح أن يقول لهم إِنِّي خالِقٌ بَشَراً وما عرفوا ما البشر ولا عهدوا به قبل؟
Answer
I say: its aspect is that He had said to them: "I will create a creature whose description is such and such," but when He related it, He limited it to the name. "So when I have proportioned him": when I complete his creation and make him upright, "and breathed into him of My spirit": and gave him life and made him sensitive and breathing, "then fall down": then prostrate; "kull" is for inclusiveness, and "ajma'un" is for togetherness, so together they conveyed that they prostrated to the last of them, not one angel remained but prostrated, and that they all prostrated at one time, not separated into different times.
قلت: وجهه أن يكون قد قال لهم: إنى خالق خلقا من صفته كيت وكيت، ولكنه حين حكاه اقتصر على الاسم فَإِذا سَوَّيْتُهُ فإذا أتممت خلقه وعدلته وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِي وأحييته وجعلته حساسا متنفسا فَقَعُوا فخروا، كل: للإحاطة. وأجمعون: للاجتماع، فأفادا معا أنهم سجدوا عن آخرهم ما بقي منهم ملك إلا سجد، وأنهم سجدوا جميعا في وقت واحد غير متفرّقين في أوقات.
Question
If you say: How was prostration to other than God permissible?
فإن قلت: كيف ساغ السجود لغير الله؟
Answer
I say: what is not permissible is prostration to other than God by way of worship; as for by way of honor and veneration, the intellect does not refuse it, unless God knows in it a corruption and forbids it.
قلت: الذي لا يسوغ هو السجود لغير الله على وجه العبادة، فأما على وجه التكرمة والتبجيل فلا يأباه العقل، إلا أن يعلم الله فيه مفسدة فينهى عنه.
Question
If you say: How was Iblis excepted from the angels when he is of the jinn?
فإن قلت: كيف استثنى إبليس من الملائكة وهو من الجنّ؟
Answer
I say: he was commanded to prostrate with them, so they predominated over him in His saying "So the angels prostrated," then he was excepted as one of them is excepted, a connected exception. "And became among the disbelievers": the existence of his disbelief at that time was intended, even if he was not a disbeliever before it, because "kana" is unrestricted in the genus of past times, so it fits whichever of them you wish. It may also be meant: and he was among the disbelievers in the past times in God's knowledge.
قلت: قد أمر بالسجود معهم فغلبوا عليه في قوله فَسَجَدَ الْمَلائِكَةُ ثم استثنى كما يستثنى الواحد منهم استثناء متصلا وَكانَ مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ أريد وجود كفره ذلك الوقت وإن لم يكن قبله كافرا، لأن كانَ مطلق في جنس الأوقات الماضية، فهو صالح لأيها شئت. ويجوز أن يراد: وكان من الكافرين في الأزمنة الماضية في علم الله.

Q 38:75–76 · Vol. 4, pp. 105–107

Verses 75 to 76

The verses as the commentary quotes them
[God] said, "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands? Were you arrogant, or were you among the exalted?" (75) He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay" (76)
قالَ يا إِبْلِيسُ ما مَنَعَكَ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ لِما خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ أَمْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الْعالِينَ (75) قالَ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِي مِنْ نارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُ مِنْ طِينٍ (76)
Vol. 4, p. 105
Question
If you say: What is the aspect of His saying "I created with My hands"?
فإن قلت: ما وجه قوله خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ:
Answer
I say: it has preceded for us that one who has two hands performs most of his actions with his hands, so action with the two hands predominated over all other actions done by other than them, until it was said of an action of the heart: "it is of what your hands did," and until it was said of one who has no hands: "Your hands tied [the waterskin] and your mouth blew" «1», and until no difference remained between your saying "this is of what I did" and "this is of what your hands did." From it is His saying "of what Our hands have done"
قلت: قد سبق لنا أنّ ذا اليدين يباشر أكثر أعماله بيديه، فغلب العمل باليدين على سائر الأعمال التي تباشر بغيرهما، حتى قيل في عمل القلب: هو مما عملت يداك، وحتى قيل ممن لا يدي له: يداك أوكتا «1» وفوك نفخ، وحتى لم يبق فرق بين قولك: هذا مما عملته، وهذا مما عملته يداك. ومنه قوله تعالى مِمَّا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِينا
Vol. 4, p. 106
and "for that which I created with My hands."
ولِما خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ.
Question
If you say: What then is the meaning of His saying "What prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands"?
فإن قلت: فما معنى قوله ما مَنَعَكَ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ لِما خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ؟
Answer
I say: the aspect for which Iblis found prostration to Adam objectionable and disdained it was that it is prostration to a creature, so he took pride in himself and was arrogant that his prostration be to other than the Creator, and to that was added that Adam is created from clay and he from fire. And he saw for fire a superiority over clay, so he considered it great to prostrate to a creature despite his own superiority over him in rank; and it escaped him that God, Glorified, when He commanded it, the most honored of His servants to Him «1» and the nearest to Him in nearness, namely the angels — who are more deserving of taking pride in themselves against humbling to the puny human, and of disdaining prostration to him more than others than they — then they did not do so, but followed God's command and placed it before their eyes and did not turn to the disparity between the prostrator and the one prostrated to, out of exaltation of their Lord's command and reverence for His address; and he, with his lowness from their ranks, was fit to follow them and tread in their steps, and to know that they, in prostrating to one lower than they by God's command, were more deeply immersed in His worship than in prostrating to him, because in it is the casting off of pride and the lowering of the wing; so it was said to him: "What prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands," that is: what prevented you from prostrating to a thing which is — as you say — a creature I made with My hand, no doubt of its being created, in compliance with My command and in magnification of My address, as the angels did; so He mentioned to him what he had abandoned of prostration along with mentioning the reason to which he clung in abandoning it, and it was said to him: why did you abandon it with the existence of this reason, when God had commanded you with it? that is: you ought to have considered God's command and not considered this reason; and its example is that a king commands his vizier to visit one of the lowly attendants, and he refuses, considering his lowliness, so he says to him: "What prevented you from humbling yourself to one whose lowliness is not hidden from me «2»," meaning: why did you not consider my command and my address and leave the consideration of
قلت: الوجه الذي استنكر له إبليس السجود لآدم، واستنكف منه أنه سجود لمخلوق، فذهب بنفسه، وتكبر أن يكون سجوده لغير الخالق، وانضم إلى ذلك أنّ آدم مخلوق من طين وهو مخلوق من نار. ورأى للنار فضلا على الطين فاستعظم أن يسجد لمخلوق مع فضله عليه في المنصب، وزلّ عنه أنّ الله سبحانه حين أمر به أعزّ عباده عليه «1» وأقربهم منه زلفى وهم الملائكة، وهم أحق بأن يذهبوا بأنفسهم عن التواضع للبشر الضئيل، ويستنكفوا من السجود له من غيرهم، ثم لم يفعلوا وتبعوا امر الله وجعلوه قدّام أعينهم، ولم يلتفتوا إلى التفاوت بين الساجد والمسجود له، تعظيما لأمر ربهم وإجلالا لخطابه: كان هو مع انحطاطه عن مراتبهم حرى بأن يقتدى بهم ويقتفى أثرهم، ويعلم أنهم في السجود لمن هو دونهم بأمر الله، أو غل في عبادته منهم في السجود له، لما فيه من طرح الكبرياء وخفض الجناح، فقيل له: ما منعك أن تسجد لما خلقت بيدىّ، أى: ما منعك من السجود لشيء هو كما تقول مخلوق خلفته بيدي- لا شكّ في كونه مخلوقا- امتثالا لأمرى وإعظاما لخطابى كما فعلت الملائكة، فذكر له ما تركه من السجود مع ذكر العلة التي تشبث بها في تركه، وقيل له: لم تركته مع وجود هذه العلة، وقد أمرك الله به، يعنى: كان عليك أن تعتبر أمر الله ولا تعتبر هذه العلة، ومثاله: أن يأمر الملك وزيره أن يزور بعض سقاط الحشم فيمتنع اعتبارا لسقوطه، فيقول له: ما منعك أن تتواضع لمن لا يخفى علىّ سقوطه «2» ، يريد: هلا اعتبرت أمرى وخطابي وتركت
Vol. 4, p. 107
consideration of his lowliness, and in it: that I created him with my hand, so I know his state, and with that I commanded the angels to prostrate to him because of a wisdom that called me to it, of favoring him with exalted honor and testing the angels; so who are you that something would turn you away from prostrating to him that did not turn Me away from commanding prostration to him. It is also said: the meaning of "to that which I created with My hands" is: that which I created without an intermediary. It has been read "biyadayya," as "bimusrikhiyya" was read, and "biyadi" in the singular. "Min al-'alin": of those who were exalted, who excelled; and he answered that he was among the exalted in that he said "I am better than him." It is also said: "Are you arrogant now, or have you been among the arrogant ever since you existed?" and the meaning of the hamza is affirmation. It has been read "astakbarta" with omission of the interrogative particle, because "am" indicates it, or in the sense of a report. This was by way of the more fitting, that is: "Had he been created of fire, I would not have prostrated to him, because he is a creature like me, so how shall I prostrate to one who is lower than I, because he is of clay, and fire overcomes clay and consumes it"; and the second sentence, which is "You created me from fire," ran from the first like the conjoined [element of] explicative apposition from that to which it is conjoined, in clarification and elucidation.
اعتبار سقوطه، وفيه: أنى خلقته بيدي، فأنا أعلم بحاله، ومع ذلك أمرت الملائكة بأن يسجدوا له لداعي حكمة دعاني إليه: من إنعام عليه بالتكرمة السنية وابتلاء للملائكة، فمن أنت حتى يصرفك عن السجود له، ما لم يصرفني عن الأمر بالسجود له. وقيل: معنى لِما خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ لما خلقت بغير واسطة. وقرئ: بيدىّ، كما قرئ: بمصرخىّ. وقرئ: بيدي، على التوحيد مِنَ الْعالِينَ ممن علوت وفقت، فأجاب بأنه من العالين حيث قالَ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ وقيل: استكبرت الآن، أم لم تزل منذ كنت من المستكبرين. ومعنى الهمزة: التقرير. وقرئ: استكبرت بحذف حرف الاستفهام، لأنّ أم تدل عليه. أو بمعنى الإخبار. هذا على سبيل الأولى، أى: لو كان مخلوقا من نار لما سجدت له، لأنه مخلوق مثلي، فكيف أسجد لمن هو دوني لأنه من طين والنار تغلب الطين وتأكله، وقد جرت الجملة الثانية من الأولى وهي خَلَقْتَنِي مِنْ نارٍ مجرى المعطوف عطف البيان من المعطوف عليه في البيان والإيضاح.
Editor’s notes on these 3 pages
Vol. 4, p. 105
1. (1) . His statement "your hands tied (yadaka awkata)": in al-Sihah: "awka 'ala ma fi siqa'ihi," when he tied it with the waterskin-string (wika'). (Ayn)
1. (1) . قوله «يداك أوكتا» في الصحاح: أوكى على ما في سقائه: إذا شده بالوكاء. (ع)
Vol. 4, p. 106
1. (1) . His statement "when He commanded it, the most honored of His servants": built on the Mu'tazilite school, that the angel is better than the human. According to the Sunnis: the human is better than the angel. (Ayn)
2. . Mahmud said: "Since one who has two hands performs most of his actions with his hands, action by the two hands predominated over all other actions performed by other than the two hands, until it was said of an action of the heart: this is of what your hands did. He said: and its meaning is that the aspect for which Iblis found prostration to Adam objectionable and disdained because of it is that it is prostration to a creature, who is lower than the prostrator, because Adam is of clay and Iblis of fire, so he saw for fire a superiority over clay, and it escaped him that God, Glorified, when He commanded the most honored of His servants to Him and the nearest to Him, namely the angels, to prostrate to this human, they did not refuse and did not go off with themselves into pride, despite his lowness from their ranks; so it was said to him: 'What prevented you from prostrating to this which is created by My hands, as occurred to you, though there is no doubt that in that is compliance with My command and magnification of My address, as the angels did?' So He mentioned to him the reason that prevented him from prostration, and it was said to him: 'What moved you to consider this reason rather than consider My command?' And its example is that a king commands his vizier to visit one of the lowly attendants, and he refuses out of consideration of his lowliness, so he says to him: 'What prevented you from humbling yourself to one whose lowliness is not hidden from me?' He means: why did you not consider my command and my address and leave the consideration of his lowliness. This is the end of what is intended from the verse, after prolonging, exaggeration, prolixity and verbosity." Ahmad said: He only prolonged the speech here to flee from two beliefs of the Sunnis which this verse comprises. One: that the two hands are among the attributes of the Essence, established by hearing [revelation]. This is the school of Abu al-Hasan and the Qadi, after refuting the interpretation of the two hands as power, for God's power is one, while the two hands are mentioned in the dual form; and they refuted interpreting them as favor, because God's favors cannot be counted, so how could they be restricted by the dual. Others of the Sunnis, such as the Imam al-Haramayn and others, permit interpreting them as power and as favor, and answer what those two mentioned by saying that what is meant is the favor of this world and the Hereafter, and this is what verifies his preference over Iblis, since Iblis was not created for the favor of the Hereafter; and on the basis that what is meant is power, the dual is for magnification, and the like of that is found in the language in abundance. The second belief: that the prophet is better than the angel. Al-Zamakhshari is intensely partisan in this issue and in rejecting those of the Sunnis who say that; no wonder he committed a wrong in extending his speech on Adam ﷺ for he likened his story, in the lowering of his rank, according to his claim, from the rank of the angels, to the king's saying to his vizier: "visit one of the lowly attendants," so he made the lowly attendants of the king an example for Adam, who is the source of the prophets, peace be upon them; and he established an excuse for Iblis and approved his belief that he is better than Adam because he is of fire and Adam of clay; he only erred, in his view, from another side, namely that he did not measure himself against the angels when they prostrated to him, despite their knowledge that in relation to them he is lowered in rank and fallen in station; and he made His saying "to that which I created with My hands" mentioned only as a confirmation of the reason that prevented Iblis from prostration, namely his being lower than him. And this — we ask God for protection — what is meant by it is the opposite of what al-Zamakhshari understood; it was mentioned only to magnify Iblis's disobedience, since he refused to honor one whom God honored by creating him with His hand, and that is an honoring of Adam, not a belittling of him. The hadith that came regarding intercession proves it, when people say to him as they go to him for it: "You are Adam, father of mankind, God created you with His hand and made His angels prostrate to you and settled you in His Paradise"; they mention that only in the context of enumerating his honors and distinctions, not in what lowers him, God forbid; and we ask Him to protect us from the pits of desire and its destructions, and to guide us to the path of truth and its ways; He is the Guardian of success and worthy of response.
1. (1) . قوله «حين أمر به أعز عباده» مبنى على مذهب المعتزلة: أن الملك أفضل من البشر. وعند أهل السنة: البشر أفضل من الملك. (ع)
2. . قال محمود: «لما كان ذو اليدين يباشر أكثر أعماله بيديه: غلب العمل باليدين على سائر الأعمال التي تباشر بغير اليدين، حتى قيل في عمل القلب: هذا مما عملت يداك. قال ومعناه أن الوجه الذي استنكر له إبليس السجود لآدم واستنكف بسببه: أنه سجود لمخلوق، مع أنه دون الساجد، لأن آدم من طين، وإبليس من نار، فرأى للنار فضلا على الطين، وزل عنه أن الله سبحانه حين أمر أعز عباده عليه وأقربهم منه وهم الملائكة أن يسجدوا لهذا البشر: لم يمتنعوا ولم يذهبوا بأنفسهم إلى التكبر، مع انحطاطه عن مراتبهم، فقيل له: ما منعك أن تسجد لهذا الذي هو مخلوق بيدي كما وقع لك، مع أنه لا شك أن في ذلك امتثالا لأمرى وإعظاما لخطابى كما فعلت الملائكة، فذكر له العلة التي منعته من السجود، وقيل له: ما حملك على اعتبار هذه العلة دون اعتبار أمرى، ومثاله: أن يأمر الملك وزيره أن يزور بعض سقاط الحشم، فيمتنع اعتبارا لسقوطه. فيقول له: ما منعك أن تتواضع لمن لا يخفى على سقوطه، يريد: علا اعتبرت أمرى وخطابي وتركت اعتبار سقوطه، انتهى المقصود من الآية بعد تطويل وإطناب وإكثار وإسهاب. قال أحمد: إنما أطال القول هنا ليفر من معتقدين لأهل السنة تشتمل عليهما هذه الآية: أحدهما: أن اليدين من صفات الذات أثبتهما السمع، هذا مذهب أبى الحسن والقاضي، بعد إبطالهما حمل اليدين على القدرة، فان قدرة الله تعالى واحدة، واليدان مذكورتان بصيغة التثنية، وأبطلا حملهما على النعمة بأن نعم الله لا تحصى، فكيف تحصر بالتثنية. وغيرهما من أهل السنة كامام الحرمين وغيره يجوز حملهما على القدرة والنعمة، ويجيب عما ذكراه بأن المراد نعمة الدنيا والآخرة، وهذا مما يحقق تفضيله على إبليس، إذ لم يخلق إبليس لنعمة الآخرة، وعلى أن المراد القدرة، فالتثنية تعظيم، ومثل ذلك يوجد في اللغة كثيرا. المعتقد الثاني: أن النبي أفضل من الملك، والزمخشري شديد العصبية في هذه المسألة والإنكار على من قال بذلك من أهل السنة، لا جرم أنه أجرم في بسط كلامه على آدم عليه السلام، فمثل قصته في انحطاط مرتبته على زعمه عن مرتبة الملائكة بقول الملك لوزيره. زر بعض سقاط الحشم، فجعل سقاط حشم الملك مثالا لآدم الذي هو عنصر الأنبياء عليهم السلام، وأقام لإبليس عذره وصوب اعتقاده. أنه أفضل من آدم لكونه من نار وآدم من طين، وإنما غلطه من جهة أخرى. وهو أنه لم يقس نفسه على الملائكة إذ سجدوا له، على علمهم أنه بالنسبة إليهم محطوط الرتبة ساقط المنزلة، وجعل قوله تعالى لِما خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ إنما ذكر تقريرا للعلة التي منعت إبليس من السجود، وهو كونه دونه، وهذا- نسأل الله العصمة- المراد منه ضد ما فهم الزمخشري، وإنما ذكر ذلك تعظيما لمعصية إبليس، إذ امتنع من تعظيم من عظمه الله إذ خلقه بيده، وذلك تعظيم لآدم لا تحقير منه. ويدل عليه الحديث الوارد في الشفاعة، إذ يقول له الناس عند ما يقصدونه فيها: أنت آدم أبو البشر خلقك الله بيده وأسجد لك ملائكته وأسكنك جنته، فإنما يذكرون ذلك في سياق تعديد كراماته وخصائصه، لا فيما يحط منه، معاذ الله وإياه نسأل أن يعصمنا من مهاوي الهوى ومهالكه، وأن يرشدنا إلى سبيل الحق ومسالكه، إنه ولى التوفيق، وبالاجابة حقيق.

Q 38:77–78 · Vol. 4, pp. 107–108

Verses 77 to 78

The verses as the commentary quotes them
[God] said, "Then get out of it, for indeed you are expelled (77) And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense" (78)
قالَ فَاخْرُجْ مِنْها فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ (77) وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ لَعْنَتِي إِلى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ (78)
Vol. 4, p. 107
"Of it": from Paradise; and it is said: from the heavens. And it is said: from the form you are in, because he used to boast of his form, so God changed his form: he became black after having been white, ugly after having been handsome, and dark after having been luminous. And "al-rajim" is "al-marjum," and its meaning is "the expelled," as it is said "the driven away" and "the cursed," because one who is expelled is pelted with stones on his track. And "al-rajm" is pelting with stones. Or because the devils are pelted with meteors.
مِنْها من الجنة، وقيل: من السماوات. وقيل: من الخلقة التي أنت فيها، لأنه كان يفتخر بخلقته فغير الله خلقته، فاسودّ بعد ما كان أبيض وقبح بعد ما كان حسنا، وأظلم بعد ما كان نورانيا. والرجيم: المرجوم. ومعناه: المطرود، كما قيل له: المدحور والملعون، لأنّ من طرد رمى بالحجارة على أثره. والرجم: الرمي بالحجارة. أو لأنّ الشياطين يرجمون بالشهب.
Vol. 4, p. 108
Question
If you say: His saying "My curse until the Day of Recompense": as if the curse of Iblis has the Day of Recompense as its limit and then ceases?
فإن قلت: قوله لَعْنَتِي إِلى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ كأن لعنة إبليس غايتها يوم الدين ثم تنقطع؟
Answer
I say: how could it cease when God Almighty said "Then a caller will announce among them: the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers"? But the meaning is that the curse is upon him in this world, and when it is the Day of Recompense, there will be joined for him with the curse that which makes him forget the curse, so it is as if it ceased.
قلت: كيف تنقطع وقد قال الله تعالى فَأَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ بَيْنَهُمْ أَنْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ ولكن المعنى: أن عليه اللعنة في الدنيا، فإذا كان يوم الدين اقترن له باللعنة ما ينسى عنده اللعنة، فكأنها انقطعت.

Verses 79 to 81

The verses as the commentary quotes them
He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected" (79) [God] said, "So indeed, you are of those reprieved (80) Until the Day of the time well-known" (81)
قالَ رَبِّ فَأَنْظِرْنِي إِلى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ (79) قالَ فَإِنَّكَ مِنَ الْمُنْظَرِينَ (80) إِلى يَوْمِ الْوَقْتِ الْمَعْلُومِ (81)
Vol. 4, p. 108
Question
If you say: What is the well-known time to which the day is annexed?
فإن قلت: ما الوقت المعلوم الذي أضيف إليه اليوم؟
Answer
I say: the time at which the first blast occurs. And its day: the day of which the time of the blast is a part. And the meaning of "well-known": that it is known to God, fixed, neither advancing nor delaying.
قلت: الوقت الذي تقع فيه النفخة الأولى. ويومه: اليوم الذي وقت النفخة جزء من أجزائه. ومعنى المعلوم: أنه معلوم عند الله معين، لا يستقدم ولا يستأخر.

Q 38:82–83 · Vol. 4, p. 108

Verses 82 to 83

The verses as the commentary quotes them
[Iblis] said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all (82) Except, among them, Your chosen servants" (83)
قالَ فَبِعِزَّتِكَ لَأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ (82) إِلاَّ عِبادَكَ مِنْهُمُ الْمُخْلَصِينَ (83)
Vol. 4, p. 108
"By Your might": an oath by God's might, which is His authority and overpowering.
فَبِعِزَّتِكَ إقسام بعزة الله تعالى وهي سلطانه وقهره.

Q 38:84–85 · Vol. 4, pp. 108–109

Verses 84 to 85

The verses as the commentary quotes them
[God] said, "The truth [is My oath], and the truth I say (84) That I will surely fill Hell with you and those of them who follow you, all together" (85)
قالَ فَالْحَقُّ وَالْحَقَّ أَقُولُ (84) لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنْكَ وَمِمَّنْ تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ (85)
Vol. 4, p. 108
It has been read "fal-haqqa wal-haqqa," both accusative, on the basis that the first is sworn by, like "God" in "inna 'alayka llaha an tubaya'a" [by God, you must pledge allegiance], and its answer is "I will surely fill," and "the truth I say" is parenthetical between the sworn-by and that sworn upon, and its meaning: "and I say nothing but the truth." And what is meant by "the truth" is either His name, Mighty and Exalted, which is in His saying "that God is the clear Truth," or the truth which is the opposite of falsehood: God magnified it by swearing by it. And both nominative, on the basis that the first is a subject whose predicate is omitted, like His saying "By your life," that is: "the truth is my oath, I will surely fill"; and "the truth I say," that is: "I say it," like the saying "all of it I did not do." And both genitive, on the basis that the first is sworn by, its particle of oath having been implied, as you say: "Allahi la-af'alanna"; and "the truth I say," that is: "and I say nothing but the truth," as a hikaya of the wording of the sworn-by; and its meaning: emphasis and intensification. And this aspect is permissible in the accusative and nominative too. It is a subtle, fine aspect. It has been read with the first nominative and genitive, with the second accusative, and its derivation is on what we mentioned. "With you": of your kind, who are the devils, "and of those of them who follow you": of the descendants of Adam.
قرئ: فالحق والحق، منصوبين على أن الأول مقسم به كالله في إن عليك الله أن تبايعا وجوابه لَأَمْلَأَنَّ والحق أقول: اعتراض بين المقسم به والمقسم عليه، ومعناه: ولا أقول إلا الحق. والمراد بالحق: إمّا اسمه عزّ وعلا الذي في قوله أَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ الْمُبِينُ أو الحق الذي هو نقيض الباطل: عظمه الله بإقسامه به. ومرفوعين على أن الأوّل مبتدأ محذوف الخبر، كقوله لَعَمْرُكَ أى: فالحق قسمي لأملأنّ. والحق أقول، أى: أقوله كقوله كله لم أصنع، ومجرورين: على أن الأوّل مقسم به قد أضمر حرف قسمه، كقولك: الله لأفعلنّ. والحق أقول، أى: ولا أقول إلا الحق على حكاية لفظ المقسم به. ومعناه: التوكيد والتشديد. وهذا الوجه جائز في المنصوب والمرفوع أيضا. وهو وجه دقيق حسن. وقرئ يرفع الأوّل وجرّه مع نصب الثاني، وتخريجه على ما ذكرنا مِنْكَ من جنسك وهم الشياطين وَمِمَّنْ تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ من ذرّية آدم.
Question
If you say: "Ajma'in" is emphasis of what?
فإن قلت: أَجْمَعِينَ تأكيد لماذا؟
Answer
I say: it cannot but emphasize the pronoun in "minhum" or the kaf in "minka" together with "those who follow you." And its meaning: "I will surely fill Hell with the followed and the followers, all together, leaving none of them"; or: "I will surely fill it with the devils and those who follow them from all people, there being no disparity in that between people and people after the existence of followers from them, from the children of prophets and others."
قلت: لا يخلو أن يؤكد به الضمير في منهم، أو الكاف في منك مع من تبعك. ومعناه: لأملأن جهنم من المتبوعين والتابعين أجمعين، لا أترك منهم أحدا. أو لأملأنها من الشياطين وممن تبعهم من جميع الناس، لا تفاوت في ذلك بين ناس وناس بعد وجود الأتباع منهم من أولاد الأنبياء وغيرهم.
Vol. 4, p. 109

Narrated by al-Tha'labi from the route of Muhammad ibn Awn: Muhammad ibn al-Musalla told us: Haywa ibn Shurayh told us, from Artat ibn al-Mundhir, from Damra ibn Habib, from Salama ibn Nufayl, raised [to the Prophet]. And al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Shu'ab, in the thirty-third, from the narration of Baqiyya from Artat as his saying; and Abu Nu'aym narrated it from Wahb ibn Munabbih as his saying.
2. . Narrated by al-Tha'labi, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Wahidi from the hadith of Ubayy ؓ.
1. (1) . أخرجه الثعلبي من طريق محمد بن عون حدثنا محمد بن المصلى حدثنا حيوة بن شريح عن أرطاة بن المنذر عن ضمرة بن حبيب عن سلمة بن نفيل مرفوعا به. ورواه البيهقي في الشعب في الثالث والثلاثين من رواية بقية عن أرطاة قوله ورواه أبو نعيم عن وهب بن منبه قوله.
2. . أخرجه الثعلبي وابن مردويه والواحدي من حديث أبى رضى الله عنه.
37
Q 38:86–88 · Vol. 4, p. 109

Verses 86 to 88

The verses as the commentary quotes them
Say, "I do not ask of you for this any payment, and I am not of the pretentious (86) It is not but a reminder to the worlds (87) And you will surely know its information after a time" (88)
قُلْ ما أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ وَما أَنَا مِنَ الْمُتَكَلِّفِينَ (86) إِنْ هُوَ إِلاَّ ذِكْرٌ لِلْعالَمِينَ (87) وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ نَبَأَهُ بَعْدَ حِينٍ (88)
Vol. 4, p. 109
"For this a payment": the pronoun is for the Qur'an or the revelation. "And I am not of the pretentious": of those who make a show and adorn themselves with what they are not people of; and you never knew me as pretentious, nor claiming what I do not have, such that I would assume prophethood and fabricate the Qur'an. "It is not but a reminder": from God, "to the worlds": to the two weighty ones [humans and jinn]; it was revealed to me, so I convey it. From the Messenger of God, may God's blessings be upon him and his family: "The pretentious one has three signs: he contends with one above him, he undertakes what he cannot attain, and he says what he does not know" «1». "And you will surely know its information": that is, what will come to you at death, or on the Day of Resurrection, or at the emergence of Islam and its spread, of the soundness of its report, and that it is the truth and the veracity. In it is a threat. From the Messenger of God ﷺ: "Whoever recites Surah Sad will have, by the weight of every mountain God subjected to David, ten good deeds, and God will protect him from persisting in any sin, minor or major." «2»
عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ الضمير للقرآن أو للوحى وَما أَنَا مِنَ الْمُتَكَلِّفِينَ من الذين يتصنعون ويتحلون بما ليسوا من أهله، وما عرفتموني قط متصنعا ولا مدّعيا ما ليس عندي، حتى أنتحل النبوّة وأتقوّل القرآن إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ من الله لِلْعالَمِينَ للثقلين. أوحى إلىّ فأنا أبلغه. وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم: «للمتكلف ثلاث علامات: ينازع من فوقه، ويتعاطى ما لا ينال، ويقول ما لا يعلم «1» » وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ نَبَأَهُ أى ما يأتيكم عند الموت، أو يوم القيامة، أو عند ظهور الإسلام وفشوه، من صحة خبره، وأنه الحق والصدق. وفيه تهديد. عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من قرأ سورة ص كان له بوزن كل جبل سخره الله لداود عشر حسنات وعصمه أن يصرّ على ذنب صغير أو كبير» «2» .
